dossier.companion:
RE4 (2023), Ashley. These are the developers' stated goals and changes, from Game Informer on 2 Feb 2023. Ampo said Ashley hiding while Leon fought, then "having her basically disappear for a while felt like a waste," and that "We wanted the game to change when Ashley is with you." Kadoi described the tension of companion AI this way: "Making an A.I., you don't want them getting in your way. But if you can just forget about them and they take care of themselves, then it doesn't feel like you're really protecting them." She has two commands, on the right analog stick: stay close or keep distance. The original's "stop/wait" command was removed because "Realistically, she would never want to be left alone in such a dangerous environment" (Ampo). They also tried something and dropped it: "At one point, we even had it so that you could grab her hand and lead her," but Ampo "thought it looked like they were too close and didn't like it" (Kadoi). Her tone was made "a little more serious," and they "strengthened the reality of her interactions with Leon. That goes for the conversation she has with Leon as they travel" (Ampo, via GamingBolt).

The mechanics, from GamingBolt and Gameranx (secondary sources):
- She has no health bar.
- Leon can no longer hide her in dumpsters.
- Damage can knock her down, and enemies can then deliver finishing blows that cause a game over.
- Enemies can grab and carry her off, and it is game over if they escape "beyond a certain distance." The exact distance is UNVERIFIED.
- Leon can send her into tight spaces to open doors or fetch items he cannot reach.
- Some obstacles need both characters.

Inverse adds that she "will even evade her would-be captors." The original Ashley "would frequently just stand still" and responded slowly to commands. Capcom has given no public numbers for her follow distance, how long she stays down, or the carry-off distance; these are UNVERIFIED. I found no GDC or CEDEC talk on Ashley's AI. The CAPCOM Open Conference Professional RE:2023 session list I fetched includes "Navigation AI System Overview and Title Application Examples" but no session on Ashley.

RE2 (2019) has no companion during play; Mr. X works as an anti-companion. Kadoi said that when Mr. X loses the player he "will walk in random routes... checking each section of the area and meticulously moving from one area to another." Hearing something or glimpsing the player makes him track "aggressively." If he goes "a certain period of time" without finding the player, "his senses do start to grow more sensitive." Gunfire draws his attention most, and picking up some key items forces an encounter.

For WOLF: Ashley is the cautionary example, because WOLF is not an escort. Take the principles (always present, never in the way, physical help with traversal, banter while travelling, few and readable commands) and leave out the escort fail states (downed and finishing blows, kidnap game over).
dossier.level_and_camera:
Both games use an over-the-shoulder 3D camera, so camera numbers do not carry over to a 2D side view. The design reasoning does carry over.

- Nakashima: "A larger field of vision brings with it a greater sense of security... this makes it harder to manufacture fear in comparison to a first-person point of view." With a wide third-person view, "sounds for anything unseen end up being far away." This supports the tighter zoom and wider (1.5 to 2 screen) rooms already decided: a camera that does not show the whole room leaves off-screen space for sound to fill.
- Mr. X turned a fixed-transition threat into a continuous one. Per Kadoi, in the original the Tyrant "mainly acted as a threat that stayed with you until you were able to successfully run and load into another section," while in the remake he "will track you down regardless of being rooms apart." Walk-through doorways between rooms (instead of load cuts) are what make that possible.
- Pacing (Kadoi, SYFY): "Constantly bombarding someone with scares can be a bit much... keeping someone off-balance and on their toes," mixing "moments of heightened terror and moments of calm."
- Safe rooms hold the typewriter and item box together. Per the Item Box wiki, item boxes "are usually found in safe rooms along with Typewriters." In RE4 (2023) the typewriter also opens weapon storage.
- Specific room sizes, camera distances or FOV values were not found in any source. Treat them as UNVERIFIED.
dossier.death_and_saves:
RE2 (2019):
- On Assisted and Standard, typewriters save for free and the game also autosaves. GameRevolution says the autosaves "kick in fairly often, and act as an extra safety net."
- On Hardcore, "Autosave isn't available... so ink ribbons are your only hope." Each manual save at a typewriter uses one Ink Ribbon. The in-game text reads "An ink ribbon. Required when using a Typewriter."
- Hardcore also cuts the inventory upgrades. Per the Hip Pouch wiki, only 3 pouch locations are marked "All" difficulties (West Office safe, Safety Deposit Room, Nap Room). Others are Assisted/Standard only.
- Background (Typewriter wiki, Unreferenced): Capcom found ribbons "too few and far between for some players who didn't have enough time," and carrying them meant sacrificing ammo or weapon space.

RE4 (2023):
- Typewriters save at any time, with no ribbons.
- Professional mode removes autosaves. GamerGuides: "Kiss goodbye to autosaves... you'll need to make sure you save your game." It also only accepts perfect parries.
- Typewriters also give access to storage for weapons and First Aid Sprays. Stored weapons keep their upgrades, which selling and re-buying would lose (Item Box wiki).
- A search snippet said an S+ rank on Professional needs fewer than 15 saves. I could not open a page confirming this, so it is UNVERIFIED.
- Whether Professional still has retry-from-checkpoint on death (as opposed to autosave files) is UNVERIFIED.

What death costs: in both games, dying sends you back to the last save or autosave. Nothing is dropped where you died. RE has no "drop unsecured items" mechanic, so WOLF//OVERRIDE's planned death model goes beyond RE. The useful RE idea is splitting saves into two layers: automatic safety checkpoints, plus a deliberate save ritual at a recognizable safe station that can be made a scarce resource on a hard mode.

Mapping to WOLF//OVERRIDE:
- Keep autosaves for position and progress, as on RE2 Standard.
- Make "secure evidence" the deliberate typewriter-style act at a safe point.
- On death, evidence collected since the last secure drops at the death spot.
- Any ribbon-like cost belongs only on an opt-in hard mode, and it must never take case space.
dossier.inventory_and_evidence:
RE2 (2019): slots
- 8 slots at the start. Each Hip Pouch adds 2.
- Most stated maximum is 20 slots in the main campaign (Inventory wiki; the Push Square guide counts six pouches for +12).
- Hardcore offers fewer pouches (see death_and_saves).
- Weapons, ammo, recovery and key items all share the same slots. Some key items can be discarded once they are no longer needed.
- Commands: Use, Examine, Combine, Discard.
- Stack sizes (wiki): handgun ammo 60, shotgun shells 30, MAG 20, SMG 200, flame/acid rounds 10, herbs 3, First Aid Spray 1.
- Item boxes share contents: anything put in one can be taken from any other.
- The RE2 (2019) inventory "is not in real time" (wiki caption), so opening it pauses play.
- Default inputs: open with Touch Pad / View / Tab; move an item with Square / X / LMB+drag.

RE4 (2023): attaché case
- A grid where items have shapes and can be rotated (L1/R1 / LB/RB / Q/E) and auto-sorted (L3 / LS / Space).
- Commands: Use, Examine, Combine, Craft, Discard, register shortcuts, attach parts.
- Stacks (wiki): handgun ammo 100, shotgun/rifle/magnum 50, SMG 100, First Aid Spray 10.
- Grid upgrades cost pesetas. The largest in the main game is "9x13 at 117 slots for 64,000 pesetas," stocked in Chapter 13 (Gamertag Mythras).
- The starting size (reported as 7x10) and the in-between sizes (7x12, 8x12, 8x13) were not fully confirmed: UNVERIFIED.
- Named cases (Silver default; Black 8 spinel; Leather 12 spinel; Gold and Classic as $0.99 DLC; Carbon and Vintage in Separate Ways) do not change grid size. Each only boosts drops of one item type, and "No source gives a percentage for any case bonus."
- The 2005 original's sizes, from the Famitsu-sourced wiki: S 6x10 = 60, M 7x11 = 77 (24,000), L 8x12 = 96 (40,000), XL 8x15 = 120 (73,000). The case is "only for weapons, weapon attachments, ammo, and health items," so key items live outside the grid.
- The fetched RE4 (2023) wiki page claims key items and treasures also sit in the grid. That conflicts with my memory of separate tabs, so it is UNVERIFIED.

Files and documents: both games present readable files that the player reads at their own pace in a menu. I fetched no source with file counts or developer comment on files, so specifics are UNVERIFIED.

Map: RE2 (2019) marks rooms by whether items remain (red if items are left, blue once cleared). This is from memory and was not confirmed in a fetched source: UNVERIFIED.

Takeaway for the evidence CASE:
- Use a small grid (fit a phone) with a few shapes.
- Keep essential progress items outside the grid so the engineer-only path can never be blocked by inventory.
- Add a one-button auto-sort.
- Give every safe point a shared store.
dossier.action_and_impact:
Hit readability through damage (RE2, Kadoi, SYFY): "The first thing we paid close attention to is the display and impact when the player first fires at a zombie." Wounds were made as "realistic and visceral as possible," a "wet gore" look meant to trigger instinctive avoidance. Damage that shows on the target tells the player the hit landed.

Impact through sound:
- Zombie sounds were recorded in a Foley studio "We used things like real meat, vegetables, and slime as materials" (Nakashima).
- Mr. X's footsteps are not real footsteps. "we recorded a lot of different sounds and mixed them all together in order to create a specific sound that would carry that level of impact that someone of Tyrant's build would create" (Kadoi). Weight is layered and authored, not recorded straight.

RE4 (2023) Professional "Only Perfect Parries will count" (GamerGuides). Frame-window numbers for parries were not found: UNVERIFIED.

Loud actions draw threats: "gun fire will catch his attention the most" (Kadoi). For WOLF//OVERRIDE, the door blast, tank drop and purge sentry are natural noise events that could alert a threat, which gives the impact kit a cost as well as a payoff.
dossier.presentation_ui_art:
- Silhouette with intent (RE2): art director Takamatsu said the Tyrant was designed from his original concept, "an infiltrator who will relentlessly pursue his target," and "This is why he hides his face with a hat" (PlayStation Blog). A threat's silhouette should state its behavior.
- Kadoi on the hat: "There are elements that we included (such as his hat) that we hoped would resonate," and "It's always unpredictable what will truly resonate with fans."
- Inventory as a separate paused screen: RE2's inventory is not real-time (wiki). Both games show items as icons in slots or a grid, with Examine to inspect.
- The RE4 case is cosmetic as well as functional: named cases and charms carry passive bonuses.
- Specific UI measurements (slot pixel sizes, font sizes, screen percentages) were not in any fetched source: UNVERIFIED.
- Painterly 2.5D parallax is not applicable to these 3D games.
dossier.audio:
From the RE2 (2019) audio director, Kentaro Nakashima (Digital Trends), and the director, Kadoi (PC Gamer):

1. Per-room reverb: "we decided to actually record the reverb we needed for every room and hallway in every stage, thus creating our own IRs," which "enabled us to modify and touch up the reverb in subtle ways." The aim was reverb that conveys a room's "size," "texture and condition."
2. Real-time binaural audio for nearby threats was chosen "specifically because of the OTS camera." The technique: "We use environmental sounds to create a quiet calmness, and then interrupt it with the binaural sounds of a nearby zombie suddenly rushing the player."
3. Environmental sounds: "we recorded and used a great deal of environmental sounds, like sudden loud noises that break the silence."
4. Game-state parameters: in Wwise they set "sounds that change based on the player's health gauge, or switching music tracks based on cues received from the game."
5. Animation-linked sound: they built "a tool that can automatically play the audio based on different values from the animation's transition data," because hand-placing sounds on animations made "the cost of changing or fixing anything... extremely high." A boss typically has "about 300-500 motions."
6. No sounds were reused from the 1998 original ("partly out of a desire to differentiate ourselves"). Tools used: REAPER, Nuendo, Pro Tools, Wwise. Microphones: Schoeps, Shure, Sennheiser.
7. Honest proximity (Kadoi): Mr. X's footsteps "aren't played separately. If you hear Tyrant's footsteps in the vicinity, you can definitely bet that he is actually in close proximity."
8. Safe-room music: the RE2 (2019) "Save Room" track (Masami Ueda; a remix of the 1998 theme) plays in every save room and, "Unlike most soundtracks of the game, this one doesn't loop" (wiki).
9. Nakashima also mentions an Audio Engineering Society (AES) paper on the binaural system. I did not find or fetch it: UNVERIFIED.

For WOLF//OVERRIDE, which uses procedural audio in Godot:
- Give each room its own hand-tuned reverb bus or preset; corridors and rooms should differ.
- Make footsteps per surface fire from animation tracks or frame events, not timers.
- Drive the engineer's breathing and the room-tone mix from health or stress.
- Let a quiet room tone hold, then break it with close-panned stingers.
- Never fake WOLF's or a threat's position with audio.
- Give safe points a distinct, non-looping cue that resolves to calm.
dossier.mobile_and_input:
- RE4 (2023) on iOS/iPadOS: "Requires iOS 17.0 or later and a device with the A17 Pro chip or later"; iPad needs an "M-series or A17 Pro chip." The listing says "We recommend playing this game with a controller" and mentions customizable on-screen controls. "Keyboard and mouse are not supported." "A limited part of the base game can be played for free" before an in-app purchase. "Save data can be uploaded and downloaded between MacOS and iOS devices."
- The RE2 (2019) iOS listing has the same A17 Pro requirement, the same free-trial and cross-save wording, and recommends PlayStation, Xbox or MFi controllers. It does not describe touch controls.
- Touch layouts, aim assist and button sizes were not described in any fetched source: UNVERIFIED.
- Console inventory inputs (wiki): open with Touch Pad / View / Tab; select with X / A / F; move with Square / X / LMB+drag; RE4 (2023) rotates with L1/R1 and auto-sorts with L3 / LS / Space.

For WOLF//OVERRIDE's hold-to-move, one USE and two choice buttons:
- Map rotate to the two choice buttons inside the case screen.
- Make auto-sort a single press.
- Avoid any drag-only interaction on touch.
- Pause the world while the case is open, as RE2's inventory does.

steal: Honest proximity audio: if the player hears WOLF or a threat (footsteps, servo whine), it is really there and really that close. Kadoi on Mr. X: 'The sounds aren't played separately.' Never fake positional cues.

Hand-tune a reverb preset per room AND per corridor in Godot (bus or Area2D reverb), the 2D version of RE2 recording an impulse response 'for every room and hallway', so the maintenance corridor, Records Access and the Service Junction sound physically different.
Let quiet room tone hold, then break it with a close, hard-panned stinger ('quiet calmness... then interrupt it'). Use it sparingly; Kadoi warned that constant scares desensitize.
Drive breathing, heartbeat and the room-tone mix from engineer health or stress, as RE2 did in Wwise with the player's health gauge.

Fire footsteps and impacts from AnimationPlayer method or audio tracks on contact frames, not timers. Capcom built a tool to play audio from animation transition data because hand-placed sounds were too costly to fix.
Layer weight sounds instead of recording plain footsteps (Mr. X's steps were 'a lot of different sounds... mixed').
Two-layer saves: frequent automatic checkpoints (RE2 Standard) plus a deliberate, ritual 'secure' action at a visible safe station (the typewriter). The secure action is what protects evidence.
Shared storage reachable from every safe point (RE2 item box: put it in one, take it from any other).

Keep the evidence CASE small and phone-readable: a few cells with item shapes, rotate mapped to the two choice buttons, one-press auto-sort (RE4 has L3/Space). Pause the world while it is open, as RE2's inventory does.
Keep essential progress items outside the case grid (RE4 2005 restricted the case to weapons, ammo and health), so the engineer-only path can never be blocked by a full case.
Optional +slot upgrades as exploration rewards (Hip Pouch +2), placed off the critical path.
Give safe points a recognizable, non-looping cue that resolves to calm (the RE2 'Save Room' theme 'doesn't loop').

A threat that keeps searching the level instead of despawning: random search routes, senses that sharpen the longer it goes without finding the player, drawn most by noise (gunfire). WOLF//OVERRIDE's door blast, tank drop and purge sentry are natural noise events.

Ashley lessons for WOLF: few, readable relationship commands (close / keep distance) instead of a 'stay here' that contradicts his character; a companion who stays present instead of vanishing during danger; physical help with traversal (small spaces, two-person obstacles); banter while travelling. Kadoi: 'you don't want them getting in your way.'
Design threat silhouettes from intent (Takamatsu: Mr. X's hat comes from the 'infiltrator' concept).
avoid: Escort fail states: no health bar for WOLF, no downed-then-finished game over, no 'carried off beyond a distance' game over. WOLF is independent, not cargo, and essential progress must stay engineer-only.
Companion-only gates with no fallback: Ashley's small-space routes are fine as WOLF's optional routes, but every one needs an engineer-only alternative.

Making save tokens take inventory space. The Typewriter wiki records ribbons were 'too few and far between' for players short on time and cost item slots. If a hard mode limits secures, keep the tokens out of the evidence case.
Removing autosave by default (RE2 Hardcore, RE4 Professional). Losing a long run's progress to death belongs only in an opt-in hard mode.
Fake or 'cheating' proximity sounds, and pursuers that teleport to the player. Kadoi conceded only that senses sharpen over time; the threat still physically walks.
Constant scares with no calm in between (Kadoi: 'Constantly bombarding someone with scares can be a bit much').
Huge grids on a phone screen. RE4's 9x13 = 117 cells suits a controller and TV, not touch at phone size.
Drag-only inventory movement (RE2 PC uses LMB+drag). On touch, use tap-select plus the two choice buttons.
Physical intimacy the characters haven't earned: Capcom cut hand-holding with Ashley because it 'looked like they were too close.' Let WOLF choose closeness through authored actions.
Copying RE's specific assets, music or Capcom names. Use the research for design principles only and credit it as a source, not a contributor.

corrections.claim: The original's "stop/wait" command was removed because "Realistically, she would never want to be left alone in such a dangerous environment" (Ampo).
corrections.problem: Misattributed quote. In the Game Informer article (https://gameinformer.com/2023/02/02/why-capcom-changed-ashley-in-resident-evil-4) this is Marcus Stewart's own paraphrase, not a quote: "Capcom wants Ashley to stay by Leon's side because, realistically, she would never want to be left alone in such a dangerous environment." Ampo's actual quote next to it is different.
corrections.correction: Present it as Game Informer's paraphrase of Capcom's intent, not as an Ampo quote. Ampo's actual words are: "As a character, we wanted to have her by your side so she left an impression", and hiding her "was fun in some ways", but having her "basically disappear for a while felt like a waste. We wanted to avoid that in the remake."

corrections.claim: Enemies can grab and carry her off, and it is game over if they escape "beyond a certain distance."
corrections.problem: The quoted phrase is in none of the three cited Ashley sources. Game Informer says "which also results in failure if they get too far from Leon". Gameranx says "you'll get a game over if they get too far away from Leon." GamingBolt does not mention it.
corrections.correction: Quote Game Informer instead: failure "if they get too far from Leon". Game Informer also says Leon can stop it by shooting the abductor or with a close-range execution, such as a knife to the neck. The distance itself stays UNVERIFIED.

corrections.claim: Leon can send her into tight spaces to open doors or fetch items he cannot reach.
corrections.problem: Overstated. Game Informer only describes "sending Ashley through crawlspaces to unlock doors from within". The item-fetching part comes from Gameranx, which was guessing before release: "to unlock doors or likely gather items."
corrections.correction: Say she can be sent through crawlspaces to unlock doors from the inside (Game Informer). Mark item fetching as pre-release speculation (Gameranx, "likely"), UNVERIFIED. Game Informer adds that these co-op barriers appear before you rescue her, which gives a reason to revisit areas.

corrections.claim: Damage can knock her down, and enemies can then deliver finishing blows that cause a game over.
corrections.problem: Incomplete in a way that matters for design. Game Informer says too many hits leave her "in a downed state where players must revive her", and it is Game Over only "if she's struck while vulnerable." The dossier leaves out the revive window.
corrections.correction: Too many hits put her in a downed state. The player can revive her, and it is Game Over only if she is hit again while down (Game Informer; Gameranx: "vulnerable for a final blow").

corrections.claim: Inverse: the original Ashley "would frequently just stand still" and responded slowly to commands.
corrections.problem: Slight misquote. Inverse (Joseph Yaden; published 23 Mar 2023, updated 20 Feb 2024) reads "she'd frequently just stand still".
corrections.correction: Quote it as "she'd frequently just stand still" and "Ashley was often slow to respond and would get grabbed in the process". Date the article 2023 (updated 2024).

corrections.claim: The RE2 (2019) inventory "is not in real time" (wiki caption), so opening it pauses play.
corrections.problem: Not supported by the cited source. The fetched wikitext of Inventory (RE2 remake) has no such caption or sentence. Its gallery image has no caption at all.
corrections.correction: Remove the quote and the wiki attribution. If you keep the claim that the RE2 inventory pauses play, mark it UNVERIFIED, or cite a source that actually says it.

corrections.claim: Walk-through doorways between rooms (instead of load cuts) are what make that possible [Mr. X tracking you rooms apart].
corrections.problem: The dossier's own inference is presented as following from Kadoi. In PC Gamer, Kadoi credits the change to AI: "the fundamental components of his AI are vastly different". He says the original Tyrant "wouldn't break through rooms aside from very specific events." He never mentions doorways or loading.
corrections.correction: Label the doorway point as a WOLF//OVERRIDE design inference. Kadoi's stated reason is the AI redesign: the Tyrant "will track you down regardless of being rooms apart from each other."

corrections.claim: RE4 (2023) S+ on Professional save limit: fewer than 15 saves (source_url: GamerGuides Professional mode page).
corrections.problem: Wrong source. The cited GamerGuides page does not state a save limit. Gamertag Mythras's difficulty guide (https://gamertagmythras.com/blog/resident-evil-4/resident-evil-4-remake-difficulty-guide) says the rank table "caps you at 15 manual saves", which is ambiguous between "fewer than 15" and "at most 15".
corrections.correction: Cite the Gamertag Mythras difficulty guide (secondary) and keep it UNVERIFIED. Write "about 15 saves maximum (exact bound unconfirmed)", not "fewer than 15". The same guide says Professional "disables autosave" and the only progress is "what you wrote to a typewriter". Whether Professional has a death-retry checkpoint is still unconfirmed by any primary source.

corrections.claim: RE4 (2023) starting attaché case grid 7x10 (70), sourced to Gamertag Mythras; intermediate sizes 7x12, 8x12, 8x13 not confirmed.
corrections.problem: Wrong source, and the sizes can be partly verified. The cited Gamertag Mythras guide gives no starting size and no prices for the intermediate sizes. Evil Resource confirms Case Upgrade (7x12) at 10,000 pesetas and Case Upgrade (9x13) at 64,000 pesetas from Chapter 13 (alternate price 44,800). It lists 8x13 at 36,000 pesetas, from the Separate Ways page.
corrections.correction: Cite https://www.evilresource.com/resident-evil-4-remake/equipment/case-upgrade-7x12 and .../case-upgrade-9x13 for those prices. The 7x10 starting size is still UNVERIFIED. A search snippet gives 8x12 at 20,000 pesetas (Chapter 4) and 8x13 at 36,000 pesetas (Chapter 9) in the main game, but no fetched page confirmed these.

corrections.claim: Background (Typewriter wiki): Capcom found ribbons "too few and far between for some players who didn't have enough time," and carrying them meant sacrificing ammo or weapon space. (Placed under RE2 (2019).)
corrections.problem: Context error. The wiki sentence is about the early games (RE 1996 era): "Capcom designers quickly found...". It is not about RE2 (2019). It is also unreferenced. On the RE2 remake specifically, the wiki says only that ribbons are needed on Hardcore, and the Ink Ribbon page says they "only appear in Hardcore mode."
corrections.correction: Put the quote under the early-series history. Mark it as an unreferenced wiki claim, not a documented RE2 (2019) design finding.

corrections.claim: RE4 (2005) sizes "from the Famitsu-sourced wiki"; the case is "only for weapons, weapon attachments, ammo, and health items."
corrections.problem: Overstated sourcing. On the Attache Case wiki page, the Famitsu citation (biohazard4 kaitaishinsho, p. 431) is attached only to the opening sentence. The size table (S 6x10, M 7x11 for 24,000, L 8x12 for 40,000, XL 8x15 for 73,000) and the "only for weapons..." sentence carry no citation. The page also gives an exception: Ada's Plaga Samples, which are key items, take case space.
corrections.correction: Call it wiki data that lists the Famitsu guide in its bibliography, not a cited figure. Add the Assignment Ada exception for key items in the grid.

corrections.claim: Digital Trends interview with Nakashima, datePublished 27 Jan 2019.
corrections.problem: Minor. The page's visible byline now reads "Published April 25, 2023", though the metadata datePublished is 2019-01-27. All the quoted Nakashima lines were checked and are accurate, including the per-room IRs, "about 300-500 motions" per boss, the binaural system "specifically because of the OTS camera", the health gauge in Wwise, and the meat, vegetables and slime Foley.
corrections.correction: Give the date as 27 Jan 2019 (metadata), with the visible byline showing a 25 Apr 2023 republish. One more detail: the 300-500 figure is qualified with "The number of animations depends on the boss, but in general".

corpus.group: Dead Space (2023 remake) and Silent Hill 2 (2024) and Amnesia (The Bunker, Rebirth): diegetic UI, checkpoints vs save points, intensity directors, fear pacing

dossier.games: Dead Space (EA Motive, remake, released 27 Jan 2023; references the 2008 Visceral original's diegetic UI). Silent Hill 2 (Bloober Team with Konami, remake, released 8 Oct 2024 on PS5/PC). Amnesia: Rebirth (Frictional Games, Oct 2020). Amnesia: The Bunker (Frictional Games, June 2023). For lineage, also Frictional's Penumbra save-spot essay (2009) and The Dark Descent Hard Mode rules (2018). RESEARCH LIMIT: the shared web-search budget for this session ran out partway through. Later sources were reached by fetching known URLs, by searching within the publishers' own sites (frictionalgames.com/?s=, gdcvault.com/browse, gamedeveloper.com/search) and through Wikipedia's reference lists. IGN, Eurogamer/Digital Foundry, the Dead Space fandom wiki and Prima Games could not be fetched (blocked, 402 or 403), so nothing from them is cited.
dossier.why_relevant: All three series face the problems WOLF//OVERRIDE now faces, with similar small-scale tools. (1) Keeping a revisited space scary after its one scripted scare: Dead Space's Intensity Director exists because 'if you re-traversed a chapter... nothing would happen.' (2) Showing state without a HUD: Dead Space shows health on the suit and ammo on the gun, and Silent Hill 2 uses radio static. (3) What death costs and where progress becomes safe: Silent Hill 2's red save squares, the Bunker's safe-room hub where you save and store items, The Dark Descent Hard Mode's 4-tinderbox save cost, the Bunker custom mode's 'saving costs fuel', and Rebirth's death-as-transformation, which Frictional publicly says did not land. (4) Pacing fear, from Frictional's '9 Years, 9 Lessons on Horror'. (5) Accessibility fallbacks: Rebirth's Adventure Mode, Bunker's Very Easy preset and 'Reduced Enemy Perception', and Silent Hill 2's puzzle difficulty set separately from combat. Together these map onto the planned evidence-drop death model, safe points, the evidence CASE, wider rooms with walk-through doorways, and procedural breathing and room tone. The project rule that WOLF's companionship should not become a crutch is supported by the absence of any combat companion in these games. They show that the engineer-only path can be the default.

dossier.companion: None of these games has a combat companion like WOLF, and that is the useful lesson. All four are built so the lone protagonist can finish everything. That supports the rule that WOLF must never be the only route. What they do offer: (1) Silent Hill 2 (2024). Endings depend on how players behave, including 'behavior toward a companion character', alongside health-item use and time spent in some areas. Source: Wikipedia, citing the IGN wiki, which was not fetched, so this is derived. So the companion relationship is tracked from many small actions, never one big moral prompt. That fits WOLF remembering how the engineer treated him. (2) Amnesia: Rebirth's unborn-baby check-ins. Frictional's postmortem says players who accepted the premise reported strong emotional investment, and some voluntarily checked on the baby beyond the prompted moments. An optional, unprompted care action works as a relationship signal, as long as the player chooses it rather than a quest marker. Frictional also admits 'we probably underestimated how big of a turn-off the pregnancy aspect would be', so a polarizing relationship premise can lose part of the audience. (3) Dead Space's A.L.I.V.E. system gives Isaac several readings of his scripted lines that match his state. The variant names 'normal, fatigued, and injured' come from a search summary of an MP1st article and are UNVERIFIED in the fetched page. The same layering applies to WOLF's lines: a line about trust can be voiced warmer or colder by memory state without new branches. (4) Silent Hill 2's radio (Lenart: it 'builds tension... and also provides helpful audio cues') is a non-character device that warns of threats. If WOLF does this job (ears, low growl), keep it as something he chooses to do. At low trust he might go quiet, but the engineer still needs another cue, such as a suit sensor click, so the essential warning never depends on WOLF.
dossier.level_and_camera: Dead Space (2023). Motive built the whole game as 'one sequential shot. From the moment you start the game to the moment you end the game, there are no camera cuts or load screens - unless you die' (Philippe Ducharme, via GamingBolt). The Ishimura became interconnected, so you can 'walk from Point A to Point Z' and revisit completed areas. Trams run without loading. Security-clearance doors and lockers were added to reward backtracking (PlayStation Blog). Backtracking is the stated reason the Intensity Director exists. Silent Hill 2 (2024). The camera moved from fixed angles to over-the-shoulder because it 'supports greater gameplay immersion and the feeling of being in the game's space' (Lenart, PlayStation Blog May 2024). The camera change forced a rebuild of set-pieces; for example, the Flesh Lip boss now starts as 'a single foe' moving through the ceiling. Senior level designer Anna Oporska-Szybisz's GDC 2025 talk (Game Developer coverage) sorted original content into 'good enough', 'almost enough' and 'not enough'. Her rule: 'try not to overdo things that only need small adjustments.' The confusing, single-colour Labyrinth was split into three areas (Rotten, Desolated, Ruined), each with its own colours and enemies. Game Developer's analysis describes 'lockable doors, open vents, breakable walls, and initially inoperative elevators' gating each building. VGC criticised the 'samey' fog and repeated corridors, saying players have to keep checking the map. Amnesia: The Bunker. Fredrik Olsson: 'a hub-based experience. In the center of the Bunker, you have your safe room', with 'the rest of the bunker... very much accessible from the outset'. Resource locations, traps and codes are randomised. A playthrough takes about 4-6 hours. For WOLF//OVERRIDE (2D side-view): treat doorways as the 'no cut' rule. Walk through them with a continuous camera pan (the parallax shift is enough) and save fades for death and chapter ends. Give each of the 1.5-2-screen rooms a distinct colour or lighting signature and one landmark, as in the Labyrinth fix, so wider rooms stay readable. Let the camera lead slightly toward an unexplored or dangerous edge. Do not adopt fog-style low visibility that makes rooms look the same.
dossier.death_and_saves: The three series give a full range of death-cost models. (A) Dead Space (2023). On normal difficulties there are save stations plus autosaves; the autosaves are inferred from coverage noting that Impossible mode disables them. Death is the only camera cut. Impossible mode: 'autosaves are disabled', one save slot that you can save to 'as often as you need', and on death you may 'continue in Hard Mode, or restart the game from the beginning' (The Outer Haven). That article says Dead Space 2's Impossible mode allowed only three saves in total; not checked against a primary source. (B) Silent Hill 2 (2024). Fixed save points (red squares). Lenart on the first save, at the well: 'This is the place where, for the first time in the game, the player can save their progress... It serves as a save point tutorial', and they moved save spots 'to unify the save spots mechanic'. He called the trade-off 'one of those game developers battles between realism and fluidity'. A save place is a recognisable piece of the world, taught once by a dedicated first instance. (C) Penumbra / Amnesia lineage (Thomas Grip, 2009). Unrestricted saving 'breaks the mood' and 'the fear of death becomes virtually non-existing'. Penumbra used save spots, autosaves 'whenever something dangerous was about to happen', a visual flash on autosave, and rotating save slots so players never see a file menu. Grip doubted the flash: it might reduce tension, or confuse players who did not know it meant safety. (D) The Dark Descent Hard Mode (Frictional, 2018). 'Autosaves are disabled, and manual saving costs 4 tinderboxes.' The same items are the light resource, so saving competes with light. (E) Amnesia: The Bunker. Saving happens only in the safe room hub, which also has storage and the generator. Custom mode (Halloween update, '30+ settings') adds 'Saving your progress costs fuel', a no-save option, 'Reduced safe room functionality' and 'Inventory remains unpaused'. Shell Shock is the hardcore preset. A 'Very Easy' preset came in 1.31. (F) Amnesia: Rebirth. Too much fear makes Tasi collapse and wake 'having taken another step in her transformation'. Frictional used these moments 'to put the player in a different location and change the monster encounters', and sometimes 'this made the path forward easier'. Their postmortem verdict: 'we could have put more effort into making the death moments more tangible and clear', and players read the failures as helpful. Grip's GDC Europe 2011 abstract says The Dark Descent removed fail-states and challenge yet stayed 'incredibly tense'. Applied to WOLF//OVERRIDE's planned model (death drops unsecured evidence; safe points secure it): this is model (E) with the save cost paid in evidence instead of fuel. Rebirth shows the loss must be visible and specific. Show the CASE spilling at the death spot and list exactly which items were unsecured, so a fresh restart is never mistaken for a reward. Teach the first safe point the way Silent Hill 2 teaches its first red square: early, unthreatened, and explained once. Put a safe point before each danger spike, following Penumbra's 'before something dangerous' rule. Keep any cost-to-save rule, such as fuel or tinderboxes, as an optional hard or custom setting only.
dossier.inventory_and_evidence: Dead Space puts its inventory in the world. Dino Ignacio (GDC 2013; Kill Screen interview) put health, inventory, weapon selector and locator on Isaac's RIG suit and in projected holograms. His rules: everything 'one click away'; show only what is needed now; 'simplify and hide'; 'A lot of UI is designed with the mouse in mind. It never translates.' Game Developer's GDC summary quotes his aim to 'remove a wall of safety between the player and the game'. In Dead Space the inventory and menus stay real-time; the remake's menu is 'projected... in real-time' (PlayStation Blog). Silent Hill 2 (2024) keeps a limited inventory (Push Square). Its map carries James's own handwritten notes on which rooms hold key items or puzzles (VGC), a diegetic quest log. Game Developer's 'Fog of Woe' claims inventory actions happen 'in real time' and that only safe rooms or the pause menu give respite. That is UNVERIFIED secondary opinion; it does not match my understanding of the shipped game, so verify hands-on before citing it. Amnesia: The Bunker uses a few slots, plus storage chests in the safe room. Items have more than one use (grenades, flares and fuel open locks, light things or drive off the Stalker). Frictional's Bunker custom mode lists 'Inventory remains unpaused' as an optional hardcore setting, which means the default pauses. Dead Space's security clearance adds locked rooms and lockers, so earlier spaces gain new value later. For the evidence CASE: make it a physical object the engineer carries. Its lid or latch shows filled slots, for example unsecured items glowing amber and secured ones dimmed with a sealed latch icon, so the 'what will I lose' state can be read without a menu. Opening it should be one press (USE hold or Pause), not a dropdown, following Ignacio. Pause by default when the CASE is open, with real-time as an optional hard setting, as Frictional did. Phone players especially need the pause. The one tool should follow the Bunker model of one object with two or three uses (for example open, distract, light) rather than a growing toolbox.
dossier.action_and_impact: Dead Space (2023): the Peeling System 'introduces layered flesh, tendons and bones that break, tear and shatter' (EA feature text via MP1st). Damage shows through layers stripped from the target, not a health bar over it. Weapon audio gained 'additional layered elements to make sure every shot sounds impactful' (Mike Dominiuk, via A Sound Effect). On PS5, haptics and adaptive triggers give each gun its own trigger feel: the Plasma Cutter trigger 'pushes back up, re-initializing for your next shot', the Pulse Rifle 'buck[s] with each round fired', and mag boots let you feel 'each step as the mag boots engage with the floor' (Vincent Wang, PlayStation Blog). Zero-g gained a 'propulsion boost' for dodging. Silent Hill 2 (2024): Lenart wanted combat to allow 'a wider variety of approaches' while 'preserving the feeling of playing as an inexperienced everyman'. Enemies were 'fleshed out... to make them more distinctive and unpredictable'; Lenart describes the Nurse as 'frantically aggressive' and the Mannequin as 'silent and stealthy' (Push Square). Reviews say the dodge gives 'extra confidence to stay close and save your ammo', but three basic enemies can still overwhelm you (VGC). Flesh Lip's scream 'can temporarily stun' James. Amnesia: The Bunker's revolver is deliberately clunky; the reload is single-round and slow, and Wikipedia quotes 'Loading that last bullet creates a strong sense of urgency' (preview source not fetched, so derived). The Stalker reacts to noise; the dynamo flashlight is loud when you crank it. Frictional's lesson 4: 'Fun gameplay is just too... fun', meaning engaging combat pushes fear aside. For the WOLF//OVERRIDE impact kit: tie each hit-stop or shake to a visible state change, such as a panel peeling off the purge sentry or a seal tearing, as Peeling does. Give each impact surface its own layered sound. Keep the engineer's actions deliberately weighty and unskilled, the everyman framing. Every loud action (the door blast, the tank drop) should have a cost the space reacts to, as with Bunker's noise.
dossier.presentation_ui_art: Diegetic UI (Dead Space). Health is a glowing segmented bar on the suit's spine. Dino Ignacio says 'The usable data should be behind Isaac' because the camera is third-person. Ammo shows on the weapon. Navigation is a line projected on the floor. Ignacio cites Dieter Rams' 'Less, but better'. Lighting (Dead Space 2023): the GDC 2023 talk by lighting lead Guillaume Goudreault lists 'systematic lighting behaviour' tied to the Intensity Director, custom light fixtures, colour grading and ACES. Lights are both art and a scare ingredient, flickering or shutting off on cue. Silent Hill 2 (2024) keeps the fog 'now for atmospheric reasons rather than technical ones' (VGC). Game Developer calls it 'a two-pronged approach that respects Team Silent's vision of the town while bringing more detail'. Lenart: 'limited visibility provides ample cover for a variety of monsters lurking outside the player's field of vision.' The flashlight is almost the only light. Labyrinth sub-areas are colour-coded. Amnesia: The Bunker shows the generator's remaining fuel on a pocket watch (Wikipedia; patch 1.15 fixed 'the pocket watch wouldn't sync properly with the generator'), a diegetic timer. Accessibility patch: closed captions, 'Subtitle Directional Indicators', reduced camera motion, a hideable crosshair and simpler interact icons. 1.31 made subtitles larger and turns camera shake off when reduced motion is on. Frictional lesson 7: 'Keep it vague... much of the horror comes from simply not being sure what the hell you're looking at.' For the painterly 2.5D look: put the engineer's health on their back or suit as a spine light the side-view camera always shows. Put WOLF's state on his body (eye or collar light). Put the evidence count on the CASE. Render any 'time left' as a prop in the world, like Bunker's watch, rather than an overlay. Use darkness for vagueness, but keep player, WOLF, hazards and interactables readable with rim light. Add a reduced-motion setting that disables shake and flash, mirroring Bunker's patch.
dossier.audio: Dead Space (2023). A.L.I.V.E. 'controls Isaac's heart rate, breathing, and dialogue' (Terry Calico, Senior VO Designer, MP1st and A Sound Effect). EA's feature text says Isaac's 'heartbeat, breathing, and exertions also adjust based on his stress level to provide players direct feedback into his mental, emotional and physical state'. These details are UNVERIFIED in the fetched pages and come only from a search summary: the acronym expansion (Adrenaline, Limbic System Response, Intelligent Dialog, Vitals, Exertions), breathing kept separate from exertion, recovery after vacuum, and multiple dialogue recordings for normal, fatigued and injured. Lead Sound Designer Jean-Francois Tremblay describes occlusion and obstruction for 'realistic audio projection' with 'more accurate sound positioning and distance attenuation and filtering'. Audio is an Intensity Director ingredient: creaking vents and bursting pipes (PlayStation Blog). On PS5, RIG sounds (item pickups, stasis refills, locator) play from the controller speaker. Silent Hill 2 (2024). Radio static marks nearby enemies. Lenart: it 'builds tension and creates a sense of uncertainty... and also provides helpful audio cues for players to base their movements on'. VGC notes the static plays through the DualSense speaker too, and that some creatures are deliberately silent to it. Akira Yamaoka returned. Game Developer cites ambient details like 'unattended windchimes that pierce the eerily pregnant silence'. Yamaoka's 2005 GDC talk on Silent Hill mood and ambience is in the Vault (content not reviewed). Amnesia: The Bark Descent Hard Mode note: 'There is no danger music when the monsters are near', which means normal modes do use danger music as a proximity cue, and removing it raises difficulty. The Bunker's 'Closed Captions' and 'Subtitle Directional Indicators' make audio cues accessible. For WOLF//OVERRIDE's procedural audio: build an engineer 'vitals' layer of breath rate and heartbeat driven by a stress value fed by impacts, chases and darkness, with slow recovery. Add per-room tone beds with occlusion-style low-pass through doorways, and footsteps per surface. Give WOLF a separate, quieter vitals layer (servo whine, breath) so players can 'hear' his state. Give every proximity audio cue a captioned or visual twin. Optionally, a hard setting removes danger stingers, as The Dark Descent does.
dossier.mobile_and_input: None of these games ships on phones with touch, so touch layouts are not applicable. Transferable input points: Dino Ignacio says 'A lot of UI is designed with the mouse in mind. It never translates' and wants everything 'one click away'; for Dead Space 3's workbench, with 'hundreds of thousands of options', his team used analog-stick 'radio buttons' refined through playtesting. That applies to a two-button choice plus USE scheme: keep the CASE and tool menus to one or two presses. Dead Space PS5 haptics (PlayStation Blog): per-weapon trigger resistance, mag-boot footstep pulses, and RIG sounds from the controller speaker. Map these to controller rumble for footsteps, blasts and the tank drop, and to phone vibration with a toggle. Silent Hill 2 plays radio static through the controller speaker. Amnesia: The Bunker's accessibility patch added hold/toggle modes for physics interaction, sprint, aim, reload, flashlight charging and health check, plus a lean toggle in 1.31. This maps directly onto 'one USE (tap or hold)': every hold action needs a toggle alternative. Also from that patch: 'Lock Code Quick Access', 'Reduced Enemy Perception', 'Aim Assist' and 'Non-Aggressive Rats'. Rebirth's Adventure Mode ('Monsters still exist in the game but they won't attack you anymore', with dark areas brightened) is a model for a story or low-threat option that keeps every route playable on touch.

numbers.fact: Frictional's horror lessons count

steal: A small Intensity Director for revisits. Each room gets a tension value and a pool of layered 'ingredients': light flicker or blackout, a steam burst, a vent creak, a fake encounter (a body, a sound, nothing spawns), or a real threat. These are Dead Space's ingredients, layered 'five, six, seven' per moment. When the player re-enters a room, draw one combination at random, never the same twice in a row. Follow the rule that after a heavy encounter the next section stays calm ('peaks and valleys'). Hard rule for WOLF//OVERRIDE: the director may only add atmosphere or optional threats, never block the engineer-only route.

No-cut doorways. Follow Dead Space's 'one sequential shot... unless you die': pan the camera continuously through doorways between the wider rooms, and make death the only fade. That gives death a distinct, recognisable cut.

Show state on bodies and props, not a HUD (Ignacio: 'simplify and hide', 'one click away', 'less, but better'): a spine light on the engineer's suit for health, a status light on WOLF's collar or eyes, filled and secured slots on the evidence CASE, and any time limit as a prop like Bunker's generator pocket watch.

Model safe points on Bunker's safe room plus Silent Hill 2's red squares. A safe point is a recognisable object in the world (for example a sealed evidence locker) that saves, secures the CASE's unsecured evidence, and gives a quiet place to plan. Teach the first one early with nothing threatening nearby, as Lenart did with the well: 'It serves as a save point tutorial.'

Make the death penalty visible and specific (Frictional's Rebirth lesson, 'make the death moments more tangible and clear'). On death, show the CASE spilling at the death spot and list exactly which unsecured items were lost, so the restart never reads as a reward.

Place safe points or autosaves just before danger spikes, following Penumbra's autosave 'whenever something dangerous was about to happen'. Keep the save confirmation small and in-world, given Grip's worry that a flash reduces tension.

Optional cost-to-save hard mode: The Dark Descent charged 4 tinderboxes per save and Bunker's custom mode makes saving cost fuel. A WOLF//OVERRIDE hard setting could cost a consumable to secure evidence. Off by default.

Engineer vitals audio in the style of A.L.I.V.E.: breath rate and heartbeat driven by a stress value fed by impacts, chases and darkness, with slow recovery and line readings that change with state. This fits the planned procedural audio and 'breathing' feel work.

Silent Hill 2's radio idea: give the engineer a proximity cue that 'builds tension... and also provides helpful audio cues', such as a suit sensor's static, separate from WOLF. WOLF can add his own reaction (ears, growl) by choice, and could stay silent at low trust without breaking the essential cue.

Pick-your-poison power routing (Dead Space circuit breakers: cut lights or oxygen). Frame the coolant-relay choice so each option leaves a lasting, visible room state, for example a dark room versus a venting room. That way the consequence is played through, not only told.

Colour-code room sections (the Silent Hill 2 Labyrinth split into Rotten, Desolated and Ruined) so the 1.5-2-screen rooms stay readable in the painterly 2.5D look. Give each wide room its own light tint and one landmark.

Bunker-style readable threat rules: 'it prefers darkness over light and can hear the player.' Give the purge sentry and future threats one or two rules a player can learn and use (light, noise, line of sight).
One tool with two or three uses, in the spirit of Bunker's grenades, flares and fuel (open, distract, light). Prefer this over a growing toolbox.

Accessibility tiers taken from shipped games: Rebirth's Adventure Mode ('Monsters still exist... but they won't attack you'), Bunker's 'Very Easy' and 'Reduced Enemy Perception', Silent Hill 2's puzzle difficulty set separately from combat, toggle versions of every hold action, and subtitle direction indicators.

Frictional's pacing rules as a design checklist: scares are spice ('you can't cook a dish solely out of spices'); expect players to 'optimize the feeling away'; keep threats vague; agency plus uncertainty beats forced scares. Use these to review each new room beat.
avoid: Uniform fog or darkness that makes rooms look the same. VGC criticised Silent Hill 2 (2024) for 'samey' fogged exteriors and repeated interiors that send players to the map. In a side-view painterly game this hurts readability even more.

Death that feels like a reward. Frictional admits Rebirth's fear-collapse sometimes 'made the path forward easier' and players read it that way. Do not move the player past a hazard on death unless the loss (dropped evidence) is obvious.
A save confirmation flash that breaks tension or is mistaken for something else (Grip's own doubt about Penumbra). Keep save feedback in-world and labelled.

Making the default inventory real-time on phone and controller. Frictional kept 'Inventory remains unpaused' as an optional custom setting, which implies the default pauses. AGENT.md also requires Pause and Back to work during dialogue.

An unbounded director that spawns threats on paths essential to progress, or repeats the same vent scare. Dead Space's stated aim is to stop players 'constantly encounter[ing] the same enemy creeping out of the same air vent'.

Making combat too much fun or too dominant. Frictional lesson 4: engaging gameplay 'counteract[s]' fear. The Silent Hill 2 remake roughly doubled its runtime with expanded fights, which reviewers felt as length. Keep the three short rooms short.

Relying on a single cue for an essential warning, such as only WOLF's growl or only an audio stinger. Provide captions or directional subtitles as Bunker's accessibility patch did, and keep the warning available when WOLF refuses to help.

Randomising codes or essential solutions, as Bunker randomises codes 'to prevent cheating'. In a short story game this breaks the public walkthrough and chapter guides that AGENT.md requires to stay accurate.

A relationship premise that splits the audience. Frictional 'probably underestimated how big of a turn-off the pregnancy aspect would be'. Playtest how WOLF's memory and refusal behaviour feels to new players early.

Copying Dead Space-scale gore (the Peeling System) or haptic features literally. Use the principle (damage shown in layers on the target) on machines and seals, which fits the agreed 'machines OK' direction.

corrections.claim: Ingredients layered into a single Intensity Director moment: 'five, six, seven ingredients' (numbers table, marked verified). Steal #1 also says Dead Space's ingredients are layered 'five, six, seven' per moment.
corrections.problem: The quote is real, but the dossier gives no speaker and misreads it. On GamingTrend (https://gamingtrend.com/news/inside-dead-space-4-released-dives-into-the-intensity-director/), Audio Director Olivier Asselin is describing alternative recipes that can follow one cue (a sound in a vent): 'for one possible outcome the player is thinking of, we have five, six, seven ingredients, or recipes, that could lead to something else.' It is not a count of elements stacked into one moment.
corrections.correction: Credit the quote to Olivier Asselin, Audio Director. Restate it as 'one setup cue can resolve into five to seven different outcomes (spawn, no spawn, vent breaks without a spawn, and so on)'. Steal #1 should say 'vary which outcome follows a cue', not 'layer five to seven ingredients per moment'.

corrections.claim: Dead Space's Intensity Director exists because 'if you re-traversed a chapter... nothing would happen.'
corrections.problem: Slight misquote, and the source is missing. The line does not appear in Gamereactor, GamingTrend, MP1st or Dexerto. It is Philippe Ducharme (senior producer) in NME: 'if you re-traversed the chapter, nothing would happen – everything was scripted and would only happen once.'
corrections.correction: Quote it as 'if you re-traversed the chapter, nothing would happen – everything was scripted and would only happen once' (Philippe Ducharme, NME, https://www.nme.com/news/dead-space-remake-has-an-ai-director-with-hundreds-of-random-scares-3329023).

corrections.claim: Bunker Custom Mode (Halloween update) adds 'Reduced safe room functionality' and 'Inventory remains unpaused'. The inventory section repeats 'Inventory remains unpaused' as an optional custom-mode setting.
corrections.problem: Neither phrase appears in the source, yet the dossier presents both as quotes. The Frictional post (https://frictionalgames.com/2023-10-amnesia-the-bunker-halloween-update-launch/) says 'Reduced safe room' and 'Game not paused while in inventory'. It lists these, 'Saving your progress costs fuel' and the save systems '(saving costs fuel, no saving)' as features 'available in the new modes' (Shell Shock and Custom together), not as Custom Mode toggles.
corrections.correction: Use the exact wording: 'Reduced safe room', 'Game not paused while in inventory', 'New save systems (saving costs fuel, no saving)'. Attribute them to the new modes (Shell Shock and Custom), not to Custom Mode settings alone. The inference that the default game pauses in the inventory still holds.

corrections.claim: Amnesia: Rebirth postmortem: 'players read the failures as helpful.'
corrections.problem: Overstated. The postmortem (https://frictionalgames.com/2021-03-amnesia-rebirth-five-months-later-and-soma-sells-1m-copies/) says players were split. Some felt the stakes as intended, while others felt 'caving in to the fear mostly led to benefits such as monsters disappearing'. Frictional also says the cost (faster transformation) 'had still occurred'.
corrections.correction: Say 'some players read the fear collapses as beneficial ("caving in to the fear mostly led to benefits such as monsters disappearing"), even though the transformation cost still applied.'

corrections.claim: Rebirth: too much fear makes Tasi collapse and wake 'having taken another step in her transformation'.
corrections.problem: The quote is accurate, but no source is given. It is not on the Steam page or on Wikipedia. It comes from the five-month postmortem.
corrections.correction: Cite https://frictionalgames.com/2021-03-amnesia-rebirth-five-months-later-and-soma-sells-1m-copies/. The full line is 'If the player lets Tasi's fear reach too high, she will eventually collapse, lose control and then come out of it having taken another step in her transformation.'

corrections.claim: Amnesia: Rebirth sales in the first five months: '100,000+', marked unverified.
corrections.problem: Under-claimed. The postmortem says it verbatim.
corrections.correction: Mark it verified: Rebirth 'sold more than a hundred thousand copies' (Frictional, March 2021 postmortem).

corrections.claim: Bunker-style readable threat rules: 'it prefers darkness over light and can hear the player.'
corrections.problem: Unsupported quote. It does not appear on the Steam page, in Frictional's announcement post or on Wikipedia. Steam says the monster is 'an ever-present threat reacting to your every move and sound', and Wikipedia calls the Beast photosensitive.
corrections.correction: Mark the quote UNVERIFIED or drop it. Use Steam's 'an ever-present threat reacting to your every move and sound' (https://store.steampowered.com/app/1944430/Amnesia_The_Bunker/) instead.

corrections.claim: Game Developer 'Fog of Woe' says Silent Hill 2's runtime grew 'from 8-10 hours to about 16+ hours' (marked derived).
corrections.problem: The figure is misreported. The article says the remake doubles the original's 8-10 hours to about 16-20 hours. VGC's review also says '16-20 hour playthrough'.
corrections.correction: Use '8-10 hours to about 16-20 hours'. This agrees with Lenart's '16-18 hours average', 'more than 20h' for completionists.

corrections.claim: A.L.I.V.E. 'controls Isaac's heart rate, breathing, and dialogue' (Terry Calico). EA's text on heartbeat, breathing and exertions is presented as part of the same A.L.I.V.E. material.
corrections.problem: Small misquote, plus a misattribution. A Sound Effect says 'heart rate, breathing, and dialogue delivery'. The EA text quoted by MP1st ('Isaac's heartbeat, breathing, and exertions also adjust based on his stress level...') sits under the heading 'The Intensity Director', and A.L.I.V.E. does not appear on that page.

corpus.group: Hollow Knight and Celeste: movement feel, death loops (shade, instant respawn), benches and checkpoints, map and journal as inventory, assist modes and the debate around them

dossier.games: Celeste (Maddy Makes Games / Extremely OK Games: Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry; Jan 25, 2018; PICO-8 prototype Aug 2015; Farewell chapter 9 added Sept 2019). Hollow Knight (Team Cherry: Ari Gibson, William Pellen, with David Kazi; 2017; Unity after an early Stencyl build). Secondary comparison: Hollow Knight: Silksong (Team Cherry, Sept 2025), but only for its death and bench changes.
dossier.why_relevant: These two games are the best-documented 2D side-view examples of the four systems WOLF//OVERRIDE has decided to build next. (1) Movement feel with released source code: Celeste's Player.cs is public, with every constant, and Team Cherry has described Hollow Knight's movement model on the record. (2) Death that changes how you treat items you carry: Celeste strawberries follow you and are lost on death until you collect them, and Hollow Knight's Shade holds your dropped currency at the death spot. This is very close to the decided 'dying drops unsecured evidence; safe points secure it'. (3) Safe points that do several jobs: Hollow Knight benches save, heal, set the respawn point, let you change charms and write explored rooms onto the map. (4) A map and journal used as an information inventory: Cornifer and the quill, map updates only at benches, Hunter's Journal entries that fill in over time. (5) Celeste's Assist Mode is the main reference in the difficulty and accessibility debate, including a public rewording of its warning text. The same text gives WOLF//OVERRIDE wording for its engineer-only and accessibility fallbacks. Both games are platformers with acrobatics the engineer will not have. Their numbers show how a forgiveness system is put together; WOLF//OVERRIDE's slower, grounded movement should not copy the values.

dossier.companion:
Neither game has a companion like WOLF who walks with the player, makes his own choices and remembers how he was treated. The closest examples are below.

CELESTE: Badeline ('Part of Me') starts as a chaser and becomes a partner. The chaser is built on a replay buffer, not on pathfinding. Player.cs keeps a list of ChaserState snapshots of the player, with ChaserStateMaxTime = 4f (the buffer holds 4 seconds). GetChasePosition(sceneTime, timeAgo) returns where Madeline was 'timeAgo' seconds earlier, with a 0.02 s tolerance. It also replays her sounds (AddChaserStateSound). The developers' Readme says ChaserState 'could likely be abstracted into a Component.' This is a cheap way for WOLF to follow, and later lead, on a delayed copy of a path that is known to be walkable. Theo and Granny are dialogue companions with no mechanics.

HOLLOW KNIGHT: no party companion. NPCs such as Cornifer, Quirrel and Hornet show up at points along your route. Cornifer is found by sound and trail: 'Humming sound can be heard across the room' and 'Scattered papers on the ground lead toward his location' (the wiki notes he goes silent in Deepnest 'out of fear'). This audio-first way of locating a character is the pattern to use for WOLF calling from a room he has scouted. Confessor Jiji will summon your Shade back to town in exchange for a Rancid Egg (Shade wiki). Silksong has an item that does the same job (a Silkeater retrieves the Cocoon 'from anywhere'). Both are 'a third party fetches what you lost' services, which maps onto WOLF choosing, or refusing, to retrieve dropped evidence.

Neither game has a companion who can refuse. For WOLF//OVERRIDE, a refusal must never remove the engineer's own recovery path.
dossier.level_and_camera:
CELESTE (source-verified): the camera eases toward its target every frame: position += (target - from) * (1 - 0.01^dt). Each second it closes 99% of the remaining gap, regardless of frame rate. The target is centred on the player plus a per-level CameraOffset, then clamped to room Bounds (level.Bounds.Right - GameWidth). Special states push the camera ahead: red-bubble dash +48 px along the direction of travel, summit launch -64 px vertical, star-fly +0.2 x velocity. CameraAnchor/CameraAnchorLerp let level triggers pull the camera toward authored points on X, Y or both. Rooms are separate screens with a checkpoint at each room start (Wikipedia: 'checkpoints between single-screen challenges'). The game's base resolution, usually quoted as 320x180, is in Celeste.GameWidth/GameHeight, which is not in the released file: UNVERIFIED. Maddy's physics article: all colliders are integer axis-aligned boxes, and fractional movement accumulates as a remainder ('positions, widths, and heights are integer numbers'). Actors riding a solid move with it, and 'pushing takes priority over carrying.'

HOLLOW KNIGHT (interviews): rooms are blocked out with black 64x64-pixel tiles, then playtested for spacing before Ari 'dress[es]' them (Gibson and Pellen, PC Gamer 2017). The world is a coherent physical space: the map is 'probably 98% pure... just a few cheats... a tiny room goes down like, 20 tiles too low' (Gibson). Pellen: 'as soon as you have areas where you go through this door and come up through here and suddenly you're in another area and it doesn't make sense anymore, you can't map it in your head.' They tried a game-jam design with randomised prefab rooms and abandoned it ('it stressed me out'). They cut the largest area, Bone Forest, because 'the game's already quite overwhelming... how much information they could retain.' They deliberately allow getting lost but put something in every dead end ('even when you do get lost you'll stumble across something'). They kept skips such as a mosquito placed in a Greenpath room so players can bounce off it. Their policy: 'leave it in, unless... a player can easily, without realizing it, get themselves stuck.'
dossier.death_and_saves:
CELESTE: on death, Die() increments session and save death counts, sets Dead, calls Leader.LoseFollowers(), drops anything held, calls level.Shake() and a Light/Medium rumble, then spawns a PlayerDeadBody (Player.cs). You respawn at the start of the current room. The exact respawn duration lives in PlayerDeadBody/Level, which were not released: UNVERIFIED. Strawberries follow Madeline and are collected only later; the wiki's 1-UP rule (collect six 'all at once' without touching ground for more than 8 frames) confirms this delayed collection. Dying with a follower loses it, because LoseFollowers() sends it back. Strawberry seeds go further: 'If you touch the ground before gathering all seeds... the ones collected will move to their original positions.' Golden strawberries raise the stakes: 'a death will result in both the loss of the berry and the player being teleported back to the room where they first obtained it.' Deaths are framed as learning. The Chapter 3 postcard reads: 'Be proud of your Death Count! The more you die, the more you're learning. Keep going!' The Chapter 1 postcard reads: 'Select Save and Quit from the pause menu at any time... You'll resume from the same screen and you won't lose any progress!' Optional collectibles are explicitly low-stakes (Chapter 2 postcard: 'Strawberries will impress your friends, but that's about it.').

HOLLOW KNIGHT: on death you lose all Geo and your Soul meter is 'limited to 66' of 99 until you recover. A Shade spawns 'at the location where the Knight has most recently died', and a map pin marks it. If you die again before recovering it, 'a new Shade appears at the new death's location and the old one disappears' and the old Geo is lost permanently. The Shade fights back with HP = nail damage x floor(maxHP/2). The Dream Nail defeats it instantly. Jiji can summon it to town for a Rancid Egg. How the Shade came about, in Pellen's words (Game Informer 2018): 'We'd already completed the Knight's death animation, which ends with his head falling to the ground and cracking. We thought it might be interesting if you had to travel back to the place you died, find the skull, and crack it open to regain your money. Then we kicked around some ideas about the skull being possessed by an enemy, or suddenly fighting back... This evolved into the idea of leaving behind a ghost of your previous life that attacks you.' Destructoid (via Wikipedia) praised it as solving 'appropriate punishment for failing, and a risk-reward system.'

Benches: 50 in the game (7 in the Dream Realm). Resting will 'Save the game' and set your respawn, 'Replenish all health', update the map if you own the quill, respawn enemies outside the current room, refill Soul Totems and Lifeblood Cocoons, and let you change charms. Toll benches cost 50 Geo (Greenpath) or 150 Geo each (Ancient Basin, City of Tears, Queen's Gardens). Steel Soul mode: 'The Knight does not respawn upon death. Once the Knight dies, the game ends and the save profile is reset'. It unlocks after one clear. Exception: dream bosses and Godhome.

SILKSONG (comparison): the Cocoon replaces the Shade. It does not fight you, you break it to recover your Rosaries and get '9 Silk', and until you recover it your silk is limited to 9. 84 benches. A patch cut some bench prices (Shellwood 60 to 40 Rosaries).
dossier.inventory_and_evidence:
HOLLOW KNIGHT's map works as a knowledge inventory you earn. You buy an area map from Cornifer, found by his humming and paper trail (Forgotten Crossroads 30 Geo from him, 40 Geo later from Iselda; maps 30-150 Geo). The Quill (120 Geo, Iselda) is needed to add newly explored rooms. 'Maps only update when you rest at a bench.' The Wayward Compass (220 Geo, 1 charm notch) shows your position. Pins (100-210 Geo) mark benches, vendors and stag stations. Gibson called the map system the hardest problem: 'The map and the mapping system took a long while to come together. We wanted players to feel like an explorer entering uncharted lands, so we knew that the map couldn't work in a Metroid-style way'; it needed 'a visual balance... that suggested just enough, but wasn't a giant mess of overwhelming detail.' Hunter's Journal: an entry unlocks on first kill ('Defeat enemies to add new entries to the journal and decipher the Hunter's notes'). The full notes unlock after more kills: bosses after 1, Aspid Hunter 20, Vengefly 45. Some entries unlock by inspecting a creature, not killing it. 168 entries, 164 counted. Completing it earns the Hunter's Mark. Silksong keeps the system (maps 40-90 Rosaries, Quill 50, Compass 70; map updates 'when resting at a bench or elsewhere').

CELESTE: there is almost no inventory. State is shown on Madeline: hair colour shows whether a dash is available (red #AC3232 when available, blue #44B7FF when used, pink #ff6def with two dashes), and her sprite flashes red with light rumble when stamina is under 20 of 110 (IsTired). Collectibles are 202 berries, cassettes and crystal hearts; the strawberry follower system above is the 'carried but not yet secured' model.

For WOLF//OVERRIDE's CASE: evidence picked up should 'follow' as unsecured, shown visibly on the engineer or the CASE. It should be secured only at a safe point, just as the quill commits map data only at a bench. A CASE entry should start as a partial record and fill in as the engineer or WOLF examines it, as Hunter's Journal entries do.
dossier.action_and_impact:
CELESTE (Player.cs constants, units in pixels and seconds):
- Run: MaxRun 90, RunAccel 1000 (about 0.09 s to full speed), RunReduce 400, AirMult 0.65, WalkSpeed 64.
- Jump: JumpSpeed -105, plus JumpHBoost 40 horizontal. VarJumpTime 0.2 (holding the button sustains the jump).
- Fall: Gravity 900, MaxFall 160 (FastMaxFall 240 when holding down). HalfGravThreshold 40 (half gravity near the apex while jump is held).
- Coyote time JumpGraceTime 0.1 s. Jump and dash inputs are buffered (Input.Jump.ConsumeBuffer); the buffer length is in the unreleased Input class: UNVERIFIED.
- Corner correction: UpwardCornerCorrection 4 px, DashCornerCorrection 4 px. WallJumpCheckDist 3 in code; Maddy's article says 'You can actually wall jump 2 pixels from a wall' and a super wall jump from about '5 pixels'. CeilingVarJumpGrace 0.05. WallSpeedRetentionTime 0.06.
- Dash: DashSpeed 240, DashTime 0.15, DashCooldown 0.2, end speed 160.
- Climb: stamina 110. Climbing up costs 100/2.2 per second (about 2.4 s of climbing on full stamina); holding still costs 10 per second (about 11 s). Climb jump costs 27.5. Tired threshold 20.
Juice in code: Celeste.Freeze(.05f) hit-stop at every dash start, with a displacement burst and Strong/Medium rumble. Freeze(.1f) on bigger launches. DirectionalShake(dir, .1f-.2f) on wall bounces and dashes. Landing squash scales the sprite to X 1.6 / Y 0.4 at maximum fall speed (scaled by Speed.Y/240). Dust burst on hard landings. Stumble animation after falling more than 50 px at maximum speed. Maddy's summary of the forgiveness list: all '10' tricks are 'centered around widening timing or positioning windows' so the game can 'feel kind even though it's very difficult.'

HOLLOW KNIGHT (Pellen, Game Informer): 'We wanted players to feel totally in control of their character at all times, so our model for movement was the Megaman and Megaman X series. The Knight has no acceleration or deceleration on horizontal movement. The jump has a lot of initial lift, releasing the button cuts vertical speed quickly, and the dash completely arrests vertical movement.' The design goal: players should feel 'any hit they take or mistake they make could have been avoided right up until the last second.' Hold-to-heal (Focus): 33 Soul per mask; first mask 1.141 s including a 0.25 s windup, then 0.891 s per mask; full vessel 2.923 s; about 1.791 s with Quick Focus. Taking a hit cancels it and wastes the Soul. Dash cooldown 0.6 s (0.4 with Dashmaster). Hollow Knight's internal speed constants and i-frame length were not found in a fetchable primary source: UNVERIFIED.
dossier.presentation_ui_art:
CELESTE: character state is shown on the body, not in a HUD: hair colour shows dash count, the sprite flashes red when tired, and there is a squash on landing. A death counter is shown per chapter, presented positively on the Chapter 3 postcard. Postcards at chapter start teach habits ('Jumping away from walls doesn't consume stamina!'). Assist Mode is a menu of independent toggles: Game Speed 50%-100% in 10% steps, Infinite Stamina, Air Dashes (Default / 2 / Infinite), Dash Assist (freezes the game so you can aim mid-dash), Invincibility (pits bounce you instead of killing you), and chapter skip. The original warning (v1.3.0.0 and earlier) said: 'Celeste was designed to be a challenging, but accessible game. We believe that its difficulty is essential to the experience. We recommend playing without Assist Mode for the first time.' The current text: 'Assist Mode allows you to modify the game's rules to fit your specific needs... Celeste is intended to be a challenging and rewarding experience. If the default game proves inaccessible to you, we hope that you can still find that experience with Assist Mode.' Per the wiki, the change answered feedback that the original read as gatekeeping. It was first called 'Cheat Mode'; Thorson found that 'judgmental' and 'continue[d] workshopping the name' (Vice). The goal was a 'fluid experience where players are safe to float around between loosely-defined difficulty levels... without judgement or implication that they aren't playing the game "as intended."' Thorson: 'Assist Mode breaks the game... sometimes that means letting go.' The Cuphead difficulty debate prompted it. Wikipedia (citing Polygon, which could not be fetched: UNVERIFIED in the original) says Berry estimated 'a couple of days' work'. Academic critique (Kaartinen 2019) discusses whether assist use 'taints the original intended game experience.'

HOLLOW KNIGHT: Gibson's hand-drawn art was scanned into Unity. The HUD is minimal: masks, a Soul vessel that cracks to show the post-death cap, and Geo. Navigation help is sold or earned (map, quill, compass, pins). Signs exist only for key locations (Wikipedia, citing Game Informer). The map is drawn to suggest 'just enough'.
dossier.audio:
CELESTE (source-verified): footsteps fire from the animation's frame-change callback, not from a timer. They play on frames 0 and 6 of the walk and run cycles, frame 6 of the stumble and frame 4 of the flip. Each step queries the platform underfoot (SurfaceIndex.GetPlatformByPriority) and passes its step-sound index to the FMOD event as a parameter (Sfxs.char_mad_footstep with SurfaceIndex.Param). Climbing handholds play on frame 5 using the wall's sound index, wall slides set a looping sound's surface parameter, and landings use the platform's land index; a landing right after a step plays a footstep instead of a landing thud (playFootstepOnLand). Dream blocks get a visual footstep ripple. Rumble is graded (Light/Medium/Strong and Short/Medium) and attached to nearly every event. Sounds are recorded into the chaser buffer so the pursuing reflection replays them. Composer: Lena Raine (Wikipedia). Who did the sound design was not verified in the sources fetched.
HOLLOW KNIGHT: Cornifer's humming, audible from across a room, is a diegetic audio waypoint (wiki). Composer Christopher Larkin was hired with Kickstarter funds (Wikipedia). No primary source on Hollow Knight's sound-design process was fetched: UNVERIFIED beyond these facts.
dossier.mobile_and_input: Neither game was designed for phone touch. Hollow Knight shipped on PC (2017), Switch/PS4/Xbox One (2018) and Switch 2/PS5/Xbox Series (2026) per Wikipedia. Celeste is a PC and console game, and no official mobile version was confirmed in the sources fetched. Lessons that carry over: (1) Celeste's forgiveness windows (0.1 s coyote time, buffered presses, 4 px corner nudges) matter more on touch, where timing is worse. Because WOLF//OVERRIDE uses hold-to-move and one USE, buffer a USE tap that lands just before a station comes into range, and keep the interaction zone generous. (2) Celeste's Assist Mode separates difficulty into independent axes: speed (50-100% in 10% steps), stamina, dash count, aim-pause (Dash Assist) and invincibility. These map well onto controller and touch accessibility settings. (3) Hollow Knight's Focus is a fixed-length, interruptible hold (0.891 s per mask, 0.25 s windup), a direct template for a hold-USE whose meaning is 'commit'. (4) Both games use a small button set (Celeste: jump, dash, grab; Hollow Knight: attack, jump, dash, focus/cast). Celeste's grab-toggle and Hollow Knight's control remapping were not verified from the sources fetched.
