AGENT.md: no game-feel claim until the route has been played.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Engineer-only fallback (WOLF's fixated bait makes it trivial, so the solo path is the real test). Phone touch target. One USE (tap or hold).

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Keep the knockdown loop at or below today's ~1.45 s and keep audio continuous across the restore. Room tone and any threat stems should live outside what _restore_beat/_sync_scene resets. Queue state changes during the fade and apply them on fade-in, as INSIDE did, instead of restarting the soundscape.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's 'scene change' creates 'the illusion of no time passing'. Every reference game pairs frequent death with near-instant retries; that is what makes it tolerable.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: The death model (safe points). Room tone in the real-feel work. The current _fail_beat already has the right shape.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Before the evidence-drop rule ships, decide which deaths may drop unsecured evidence. Proposal for Nathanial: put a safe point immediately before every set piece (sentry lane, tank drop, exit bolt) so chase and timing deaths cost only the replay. Make evidence lost elsewhere recoverable where the engineer died rather than gone for good. Show what is unsecured before a threat beat begins.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: No reference charges any resource on death. Reviewers still called free instant deaths frustrating ('never ceases to be frustrating, especially during chase sequences'; 'insta-fail stealth grates'), and about 95% of finishers die at least once. A cost on top of chase deaths will read as punishment unless every one of those deaths can be read in advance.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Directly shapes the decided death model (dying drops unsecured evidence; safe points secure it) and the evidence CASE.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Split the impact budget into tiers. Reserve full trauma, hit-stop and flash for authored climaxes: today the door blast and tank hit both use trauma 1.0 plus hit-stop, and the knockdown uses 0.6 plus hit-stop. Drive everyday impacts (landing after the new height change, heavy doors, footsteps) from a character effect-state analyzer that reads velocity along the surface normal. Use a soft exhale on a light landing and a grunt on a hard one, with no camera shake.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE builds weight from state changes (landImpact, breath on landing per the Wwise Tour 2016 deck) rather than from screen effects. No reference documents shake or hit-stop values. Restraint keeps the big beats big.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Existing impact kit. The decided real-feel work (weight, breathing, footsteps per surface). One walkable height change per room. Reduced Motion already removes shake and hit-stop.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Give each threat state-driven audio stems: idle job, alerted, pursuit, and a 'listening' duck when the engineer is in the ARM PANEL alcove while the sentry is near. When several threats are present, follow the most aggressive one. Give threats an idle sound that carries off screen, because 1.5-2 screen rooms will push them out of frame.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Lilja's state stems, listening-state duck and most-aggressive rule ran without a HUD, and his off-screen 'sonic identifiers' covered gaps where the camera did not show the enemy.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Procedural audio. Wider rooms. No-HUD presentation. The current alcove cover (COVER_MIN_X..COVER_MAX_X) is already a hiding spot.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Structure each wide room as quiet, then threat, then release, in roughly a 1-3 minute chunk. Make sure the walking between beats contains a WOLF decision or a piece of evidence; when the room is meant to be quiet, keep it deliberately still.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE chunks puzzles at 1-3 min per ~100 m. Planet of Lana was criticised for 'uneventful running', and its sequel added pace variation so intense sequences 'land with greater impact'.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Wider rooms (1.5-2 screens) with walk-through doorways. WOLF's own scouting and leading routes can fill the quiet stretches.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: In action beats, WOLF must visibly react within a beat (head turn, ear flick, servo whine), even when he refuses. When he scouts or leads during a threat, he should never block or slow the engineer.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Six was praised as reliable ('never ... fighting the underlying code') and criticised only for lag ('would take too long to take a cue'). Refusal should read as a choice, not as AI latency.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: WOLF as an independent companion. WOLF's own routes. Memory gating of his help.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Design the one tool so a miss costs time or position, not a death. For example, a stun or jam that buys seconds, with a clear wind-up the player can see. Do not make it a precise-timing weapon whose miss is fatal.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Little Nightmares II's deliberately weak melee worked in tone, but its 'if you miss it's instant death' outcome was the most criticised part. The tank drop already does this well: a miss costs a 6 s rewind and a coolant cloud.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Decided evidence CASE plus one tool. The engineer-only rule (the tool must not be required at a timing window touch cannot hit).

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Add an optional rumble heartbeat during sentry pursuit and offer a way to skip or simplify any timing-heavy set piece in settings, alongside the existing Reduced Motion.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Little Nightmares used heartbeat haptics in chases. Planet of Lana shipped with a QTE toggle, and Family Gaming Database counts optional screen shake and frequent checkpoints as accessibility features.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: The impact kit already has rumble and haptics. Controller and phone targets.

conflicts_with_decisions: The death model where dying drops unsecured evidence: every reference in this corpus (Limbo, INSIDE, Little Nightmares I/II, Planet of Lana, and Stray per its truncated summary) charges nothing for death. Reviewers still found free instant deaths frustrating in chases and stealth. The research argues that chase and timing deaths in particular should not drop evidence, or should be preceded by a safe point. Nathanial decides.

The impact kit's heavy screen effects (trauma 1.0 shake, hit-stop and white flash on several beats; hit-stop plus a red wash on every knockdown): no reference documents using shake or hit-stop, and Playdead's stated habit is restraint ('Turn it Down 90%'). This argues for fewer full-strength uses, not for removing the kit. It sits in tension with the 'Blowback action slice' direction, which Nathanial owns.

Sentry chase speed (230 px/s) is faster than the engineer's walk (190 px/s), and chase starts on the first frame of sight: Little Nightmares chases are survivable because each has an authored end line and a readable alert. This is current code rather than a listed decision, but under an evidence-drop death model an instant, faster-than-you pursuit is the case the research warns against.
Wider 1.5-2 screen rooms will put threats off camera: Little Nightmares solved this with audio, which means threat-state stems and off-screen sounds become required, not optional, once rooms widen.
Corpus limitation: the Stray dossier and any dossiers after it were cut off in the input, so Stray's action, chase (Zurks) and Defluxor details could not be used beyond the one-line summary.

syn.dimension: PRESENTATION, UI AND ART DIRECTION: 2.5D layering, readable characters on painterly backgrounds, diegetic vs non-diegetic UI, menus and title screens, colour and light as storytelling, character animation weight. (Synthesised from the Playdead, Tarsier, Wishfully and BlueTwelve dossiers with their fact-check corrections applied. The Stray dossier reached this pass cut off after its 'why_relevant' and source list, so Stray claims are limited to that summary text.)

principles.principle: Sell depth with fog, value and silhouette layers, not with the number of parallax planes. Keep a fixed side camera that only scrolls, and frame each room like a stage.
principles.evidence: INSIDE GDC 2016 rendering talk (Gjøl/Svendsen): the camera "typically points inwards to the screen and only scrolls"; "Many of the initial scenes in the game were literally just fog + silhouettes"; "Simple linear fog!" clamped to a maximum so bright lights "bleed through"; local fog volumes add light caught by fog rather than adding fog; water displacement spans only 6-12 m from the near clip because "you hardly notice the parallax or depth after a certain point" (https://github.com/playdeadgames/publications/blob/master/INSIDE/rendering_inside_gdc2016.pdf). Planet of Lana: black foreground silhouettes create "the feeling of looking into a set-piece or theater stage", and Stjärnljus says the fixed side view makes it "much easier to control the camera framing and stage of each scene" (Game Developer art Q&A). Little Nightmares began as a 2012 'dollhouse' tech demo of cross-section rooms (Mervik, PS Blog 2016).

principles.principle: Make the protagonist and companion read against the painterly world through deliberate contrast in shape, colour and value, and protect that contrast with cheap lighting tricks.
principles.evidence: Mervik (PS Blog 2017): Six is "stark colour, small frame, and clean, simple shapes" against a world that is "outsized", "more organic in shape, and presented in a totally different colour palette." Planet of Lana: Lana's costume was redesigned to "pop more against the backgrounds" (Game Developer art Q&A). Enemies are dense black silhouettes that "immediately pop off the screen against its colourful backgrounds" (RPS). INSIDE: characters get "a fake ambient color, that's always there, so we can see it in the dark" and a depth-edge rim light, "like the boy and all the other NPCs. It helps them fit together" (GDC 2016 rendering).

principles.principle: Ground every character on its surface with a contact shadow so depth and height can be judged. Ambiguous depth kills players and gets blamed on the game.
principles.evidence: INSIDE uses soft projected shadow decals "Anchored to boy's feet... giving a very OOT blob shadow look", plus per-bone multiplicative AO decals (about 256 in a 16-character scene) instead of SSAO (GDC 2016 rendering). Planet of Lana uses hidden 'shadow planes' so 2D trees cast 3D-looking shadows (Game Developer art Q&A). Little Nightmares' most repeated criticism is depth: "you'll inevitably misjudge your position and perish" (Push Square LN1 review). The LN2 version, "The small Z-axis means it's really easy to get slightly the wrong angle when jumping", is from PlayStation LifeStyle (corrected attribution).

principles.principle: Carry state on animation, light and sound, not on a HUD. UI that does appear is contextual and anchored in the world, and only exists while it is actionable.
principles.evidence: Limbo/INSIDE: per Game Developer's report of Carlsen's GDC Europe 2010 talk, the director set a no-tutorial-text rule; Carlsen: "we didn't want to have any in-game menus or anything." Lilja (Sound Architect): "There's no graphical user interface at all in Little Nightmares... so there was a lot of weight on animation and audio to communicate to the player what the enemies are up to." Planet of Lana: a Y prompt pops over Mui's actions; the pointer is a world-space cursor that "will also smartly snap to particular points of interest"; an animated icon showing Mui's direction and status appears only when she is separated (Xbox Wire, Wishfully). GamesRadar: "if you're standing in a good spot... the button prompt will automatically appear above it." Stray shipped with no HUD and diegetic prompts (dossier summary).

principles.principle: Build the art from one guiding image, keep it grounded, and let the threat's look come first. Hybrid 2D/3D construction is the norm, not a compromise.
principles.evidence: Planet of Lana: a 2017 Photoshop painting "has been our guiding star style-wise since then". The game is "not making a full 2D game and we're not making a full 3D game... a mix of a lot of sprites and 3D": hand-painted textures on 3D geometry, 2D foliage sprites, "a hand-painted baked lighting solution", and a wind system "to tie the style together". Art director Chan: going "a little more alien... such as the trees... didn't quite work. We need to have [environments] closer to Earth to make it believable" (Creative Bloq). Lilja: "The visual concepts of the enemy characters always came first." Limbo: "The first thing we had was the graphics... The gameplay was the big concern" (Patti).

principles.principle: Use light and colour to give each space its own identity and to mark story progress, and use restraint so tone comes from suspense rather than gore or jump scares.
principles.evidence: Little Nightmares II's mixed outdoor and indoor areas "allowed the team play much more with different lighting setups" (Lucas Roussel, Bandai Namco producer, Xbox Wire). Planet of Lana assigns each biome a palette ("lush green hills... deep blue expanse of the sea... golden sands", Xbox Wire). Limbo is monochrome with film grain and focused lighting. Mervik: "We knew we didn't want to go down that well-trodden path of gore and violence and jump scares" (PCGamesN). INSIDE adds TPDF/blue-noise dithering after every pass to stop banding in dark gradients: "Spectacularly easy to add".

principles.principle: Let the world visibly remember what the player did. Cheap persistent visual changes carry relationship memory better than UI meters.
principles.evidence: INSIDE's Huddle shader fades in bruises, burns and blood from 9 of its 26 rigidbodies as the player abuses it (GDC 2017 Huddle Up). In Little Nightmares, the Nomes you hugged gather on the staircase in the ending (Fandom; 12 are hugged and the 13th is eaten, per the correction). Stray's 27 collectible memories double as the companion's memory (dossier summary).

principles.principle: Put weight in additive presentation layers (breath, look-at, landing reaction, velocity-matched stride), never in input latency. Animation-first movement that delays control is the most-criticised failure in this genre.
principles.evidence: INSIDE's boy stacks loops, blending, simulation, and layers for 'breathe' and 'look around' over locomotion (Grøntved/Fasterholdt slides); each breath callback "controls additive breathing animation, affecting boy pose" (Wwise Tour 2016). Huddle leg animation speed is driven by physics velocity "so the feet will not slide". Limbo's boy "can look forward in time half a second to see what's out there" to place his hands (Jensen, Hanging in Limbo). Against this: Planet of Lana's "Lana's movement feels noticeably floaty" (RPS) and "animation fidelity over fluidity" (Push Square). Little Nightmares' "uncomfortably long trigger holds" (Push Square LN1). Wishfully dropped pure 2D frame-by-frame grid movement after "early feedback from publishers that were harsh but ultimately made a lot of sense to us" (Game Developer art Q&A, corrected framing).

principles.principle: A companion reads as alive through constant small body language and visible decision-making, and through rough limbs and feedback added early.
principles.evidence: Planet of Lana: a pre-jump "butt wiggle" (RPS) and "you can pet Mui at any time" (GamesRadar). Eriksson: body language alone was not enough, "we decided that we needed one more layer of emotional expression" (Game Developer). Little Nightmares II negative: Six "would take too long to take a cue/get into position" (Shacknews). Huddle: the team "had to tweak for feel by observing the expression of the total system", and on adding "hand drawn stick arms!": "It does not take much to completely change the perception."

principles.principle: Effects are tuned down, not up. Restraint is the house style of every reference game, and layered feedback is cut until it stays readable when several events happen at once.
principles.evidence: Playdead's VFX talk is titled "Turn it Down 90%" (Control Conference 2016, title only), and no Playdead source documents screen shake, hit-stop or flash. INSIDE split fog haze and tight-light glow into separate passes because a combined pass "interfered too much". Planet of Lana's flying-robot sound: "we just got rid of 80% of them" (layers; Ameglio). Family Gaming Database lists Planet of Lana under 'No Screen Shake', meaning shake is absent or can be disabled (corrected definition).

principles.principle: On phones, presentation fails first through darkness and thumb occlusion. Brightness and contextual-button visibility have to be engineered and tested on device.
principles.evidence: INSIDE iOS fitted a polynomial brightness curve to "Get it BRIGHT enough" (Gjøl, Shipping on iOS), yet iMore still found the iPhone image "so dark that I can't tell whether there is something to interact with". AppUnwrapper: "Covering up any element of the screen with your thumb does a disservice to Inside's immaculate visual language." Planet of Lana mobile patch 1.0.5 fixed "button disappearance during environmental interactions" and added "button visual feedback in menus" (App Store history). Playdead diffed screenshots taken "every 5 meters" at "around 1300 locations" to keep platform parity.

principles.principle: Menus and title screens extend the world. Gameplay stays menu-free, and the title shows a place rather than a HUD.
principles.evidence: Evidence here is thin. Carlsen: "we didn't want to have any in-game menus or anything." Little Nightmares II's main menu shows the Pale City shore rather than the protagonist (Fandom, secondary). Planet of Lana's single concept painting attracted the composer and the Xbox deal before a game existed, so key art did the work of a title screen. No fetched source gives title-screen design rules, so treat this principle as weakly supported.

targets.metric: Camera behaviour in gameplay rooms
targets.target: Side-on, scroll only (no rotation or orbit) during play; zoom changes only at authored beats
targets.basis: INSIDE camera "typically points inwards to the screen and only scrolls" (GDC 2016 rendering). LN2's added top views coincided with depth-misjudgement complaints (PSLS). Derived.

targets.metric: Contact grounding
targets.target: 100% of characters (engineer, WOLF, sentry, any NPC) show a soft contact shadow on every walkable surface, including both levels of each room's height change
targets.basis: INSIDE foot-anchored shadow decals; LN depth deaths ("misjudge your position and perish", Push Square LN1). Derived target.

targets.metric: Character visibility in darkest room areas
targets.target: Engineer and WOLF silhouettes stay distinguishable from the background at every point of every room on a phone at default brightness (fake ambient floor plus rim light), checked by screenshot
targets.basis: INSIDE "fake ambient color, that's always there" plus depth-edge rim light; iMore "so dark that I can't tell whether there is something to interact with". Derived; no numeric contrast ratio exists in the sources.

targets.metric: HUD elements during normal play
targets.target: 0 persistent HUD elements; prompts appear only in USE range, and the WOLF direction/status indicator appears only when WOLF is off-screen
targets.basis: Limbo/INSIDE/LN no HUD; Planet of Lana's contextual prompt and separated-only Mui status icon (Xbox Wire); Stray no HUD (dossier summary).

targets.metric: Prompt auto-appearance
targets.target: When the engineer stands in a valid USE spot, the prompt appears without aiming or cycling
targets.basis: GamesRadar on Planet of Lana's pointer fallback: "the button prompt will automatically appear above it".

targets.metric: Foot sliding
targets.target: 0 visible foot slide: walk playback speed = actual velocity / authored stride speed, for the engineer and WOLF
targets.basis: Huddle legs driven by physics velocity "so the feet will not slide" (GDC 2017).

targets.metric: Look-at anticipation
targets.target: Head/look-at leads toward the next interactable or hazard by about 0.5 s
targets.basis: Limbo's boy "can look forward in time half a second" (Jensen, Hanging in Limbo). Limbo used this for hand placement; applying it to look-at is a derived adaptation.

targets.metric: Input-to-motion latency from animation
targets.target: No animation blend may delay the start of movement or USE; tune animation to input, never the reverse
targets.basis: Planet of Lana "floaty" (RPS), "animation fidelity over fluidity" (Push Square). No published millisecond figure, so the threshold is UNVERIFIED and should be set by hands-on play.

targets.metric: Screen shake / flash accessibility
targets.target: Screen shake and flash each have an off option before the first public build
targets.basis: FGDB 'No Screen Shake' (absent or can be disabled) for Planet of Lana; Planet of Lana launched with only a QTE toggle and was criticised (Windows Central).

targets.metric: Banding in dark gradients
targets.target: No visible banding in fog/gradient backgrounds on desktop or phone (dither applied on low-precision passes)
targets.basis: INSIDE TPDF/blue-noise dithering after every pass (GDC 2016 rendering).

targets.metric: Flipbook repetition
targets.target: Looping sprite flipbooks (sparks, steam, coolant) never repeat a frame back-to-back; use sequential column + random row selection
targets.basis: INSIDE fire: pure random had "an 11% chance of hitting the same one twice, which looks like a pop" (GDC 2016 rendering).

targets.metric: Visual parity QA
targets.target: A scripted route screenshot every ~half screen per room on desktop and phone, diffed against reference images before release
targets.basis: INSIDE: screenshot "every 5 meters", ~1300 locations (Shipping on iOS). The half-screen spacing for 1.5-2 screen rooms is derived.

targets.metric: Content kept vs cut
targets.target: Expect to cut a large share of presentation ideas (Limbo ~70% of conceived content discarded)
targets.basis: Jensen/Patti, Hanging in Limbo. Indicative, not a quota.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Rebuild room depth around 3-4 value bands (black foreground silhouette frame, gameplay plane, fogged midground, flat backdrop) with linear fog clamped so emissive station lights, the sentry beam and the coolant relay bleed through, before adding more Parallax2D layers.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE got its depth from "fog + silhouettes" and a fog clamp; Planet of Lana from foreground silhouettes as a theatre stage. These are cheaper and more readable on a phone than many parallax planes.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Fits the painterly 2.5D look and the decided wider 1.5-2 screen rooms. Shared immutable backdrop/fog layers can be reused across rooms (INSIDE's Environment/Backdrop vs Gameplay split).

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Add a soft contact shadow under the engineer, WOLF and the sentry, a constant ambient floor and a rim light so the characters never vanish into the painted dark.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's shadow decals, fake ambient and depth-edge rim light; LN's depth-misjudgement deaths; iMore's too-dark iPhone complaint.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Required before the decided one walkable height change per room ships. Also protects the death model: a death the player blames on unreadable depth will feel unfair when it costs unsecured evidence.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Write a protagonist/companion/world contrast rule into the art direction: engineer and WOLF get simple shapes and a palette accent the station never uses; threats read as dense dark silhouettes; the station stays grounded industrial, not alien.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Mervik's Six vs Maw contrast; Lana's costume redone to pop; Lana's black machine silhouettes; Chan's lesson that too-alien environments 'didn't quite work'.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Fits the painterly look and keeps the engineer as the sole readable playable figure. WOLF being robotic gives a natural accent (eye/status light) to reserve.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Audit the impact kit (shake, hit-stop, flash): set defaults low, reserve flash for real state changes (door blast, tank drop, exit bolt), make sure three simultaneous events stay readable, and add Settings toggles for shake and flash.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Playdead's restraint ("Turn it Down 90%"; no documented shake/hit-stop), Planet of Lana's 80% layer cut, and the FGDB no-screen-shake option.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Keeps the existing kit but tunes it. Matches AGENT.md 'a small number of coherent reactions' tied to real state. Settings already use the terminal look, so the toggles go there.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Make all interaction UI world-anchored and contextual: station labels and USE/choice prompts appear only in range, choice text stays player-paced, and WOLF's direction/mood indicator appears only when he is off-screen on scouting or leading routes.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: No-HUD precedent across Limbo, INSIDE, LN and Stray; Planet of Lana's contextual prompt plus separated-only companion status icon is the closest fit to a companion that leaves the frame.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Directly supports the decided WOLF routes (scouting, leading) in rooms wider than one screen, and the 'dimensional UI/2.5D' direction. Keeps AGENT.md's readable-station and player-paced-choice rules by showing labels on proximity rather than removing them.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Keep the evidence CASE out of the gameplay view: show it diegetically (the engineer's case/WOLF's display, items visible in-world, dropped evidence lying where the engineer died) and open the full CASE only in Pause.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: None of the reference games has an inventory HUD. Stray's tiny inventory and memories live with the companion. Limbo's director "insisted on having very few elements and no inventory" (Jensen; corrected attribution).
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Serves the decided CASE + one tool and the drop-on-death/secure-at-safe-point model, which needs the dropped evidence to be visible in the world so recovery is legible.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Layer character weight as additive animation: breath (chest/shoulder pose from breath events), look-at toward the next interactable/hazard about 0.5 s early, a landing reaction scaled by fall height on the height change, and stride playback scaled to velocity. Never gate movement or USE behind a blend.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's breathe/look-around additive layers and breath-driven pose; Huddle velocity-matched legs; Limbo's half-second look-ahead; Planet of Lana's 'floaty' and 'fidelity over fluidity' criticism.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Is the visual half of the decided 'real feel' (weight, breathing, look-at) and fits hold-to-move. Feel claims need a hands-on play of the route, per AGENT.md.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Give WOLF continuous idle body language (ear/head turns, settling, servo/whine tells) and a visible 'deciding' beat whenever he helps, disagrees or refuses, so slowness reads as choice.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Planet of Lana's butt wiggle and petting carried attachment; Shacknews flagged Six's slow cues as 'wonky'; Huddle: adding rough limbs early "completely change[s] the perception."
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Matches AGENT.md (show an authored action or reaction, not only dialogue) and the decided WOLF routes. The refusal stays readable while the engineer-only path remains open.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Show WOLF's memory of the engineer in visuals: persistent grime/scorch/damage masks, posture or distance changes, and callbacks where earlier kindnesses or cruelties reappear in later rooms.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's Huddle damage shader from 9 of 26 bodies; LN's hugged Nomes returning in the ending.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Directly supports 'WOLF remembers how the engineer treated him' and WOLF memory gating, without adding a UI meter or a new system.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Give each room a distinct light key and palette shift (corridor cold maintenance light, Records Access screen glow, Service Junction hazard light) and add blue-noise/ordered dithering to fog and gradients.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: LN2 varied lighting by space; Planet of Lana biome palettes; INSIDE dithering removes banding in dark gradients.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Fits the three current rooms and the wider rooms. Light changes can also mark safe points where evidence is secured (a story-legible 'secured' light state).

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Phone presentation pass: a brightness/gamma setting with a calibration image, on-screen controls placed away from interactables and threats, contextual buttons that never vanish mid-interaction, and a scripted screenshot route compared desktop vs phone.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's iOS brightness curve still drew 'too dark'; AppUnwrapper on thumbs covering the art; Planet of Lana's mobile patch for disappearing buttons; Playdead's 5 m screenshot parity tool.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Required by the phone-touch target and the decided tighter zoom. Device checks are separate evidence from desktop renders (AGENT.md).

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Make the title screen a quiet, live view of the station (a key-art composition from one guiding painting) with no protagonist HUD. Keep the in-game changelog in the title/pause flow, never during play.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Planet of Lana's guiding painting; LN2's world-first menu; Carlsen's no in-game menus. This evidence is thin.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Matches AGENT.md (title keeps the game presentation; terminal look only for Settings) and the decided in-game changelog.

conflicts_with_decisions: Evidence CASE inventory plus one tool: the research leans against inventories. Limbo's director "insisted on having very few elements and no inventory" (Jensen, Hanging in Limbo; corrected attribution); Little Nightmares, INSIDE and Planet of Lana ship with none, and Stray's is deliberately tiny. This does not forbid the CASE, but the presentation evidence says to keep it diegetic or pause-only and make each item change a scene or a WOLF reaction. Nathanial decides.

Impact kit (shake, hit-stop, flash): no reference game in the corpus documents screen shake, hit-stop or flash; Playdead's VFX talk is titled "Turn it Down 90%" and Planet of Lana is catalogued as 'No Screen Shake' (absent or can be disabled). The research argues for heavy restraint and an off toggle, not removal. Nathanial decides.

Death drops unsecured evidence: every reference game presents death as free and instant with no visual consequence. There is no presentation precedent for showing lost resources, so the dropped evidence must be made legible in the world (visible where it fell, visibly secured at safe points), or the drop will read as punishment. Nathanial decides.

One walkable height change per room: Little Nightmares' shallow-depth rooms drew repeated complaints about misjudging position and dying, and LN2's added top/in-depth camera views did not fix it. The research does not argue against height changes, but it does warn that they need contact shadows and a strictly side-on read.

Wider 1.5-2 screen rooms: Little Nightmares deliberately frames less than the room and covers the gap with audio, which supports the decision. Planet of Lana's 'uneventful running' criticism warns that extra width needs a visual or choice beat, not just more painted scenery.

AGENT.md's readable-station labels and player-paced choice text vs the zero-HUD precedent: the reference games show no text UI at all. The reconciliation used here is proximity-only labels and player-paced choices, so AGENT.md (the explicit project rule) is kept. Flagged so Nathanial can confirm.

syn.dimension: AUDIO: footsteps and Foley, room tone and reverb, silence, music vs ambience, audio-driven animation, mixing for laptop and phone speakers. Synthesised from the Playdead (Limbo/INSIDE), Tarsier (Little Nightmares 1/2), Wishfully (Planet of Lana) and BlueTwelve (Stray) dossiers, with their corrections applied. The Stray dossier reached me truncated. Only its summary lines are usable (foley for 28 surfaces, recorded per surface; the engine's own audio with no middleware), and its detailed audio section was not available. I read the current game state from apps/game/scripts/sfx_bank.gd, main.gd and game_settings.gd. The game has 12 procedural clips (mono, 22.05 kHz, deterministic seed, every clip normalised to a -6 dB peak) and 4 one-shot voices plus 4 named loops (hiss, hum, servo, winch). Buses are Master, Music, Effects and Voice. hum and hiss follow the pressure gauge. There are no footsteps, no per-room tone, no breathing and no music.

principles.principle: Ambience and room tone are the default soundtrack; music is rare and placed by hand like a film score ("spotted"), not looped to fill space.
principles.evidence: Limbo: Andersen kept the "notional silence" instead of adding an orchestral spooky score, and turned sound effects into 'music' (GDC 2011 slides; Designing Sound 2011). HG101 counts "only six tracks" over a 3-4 h game. Planet of Lana: Furukawa says the score was 'spotted' with Klas Eriksson "as would be done in the case of films" and that "the world of Novo would be very quiet" (Laced Records). Furukawa himself urged no music on the beach run past the giant robot 'collector legs' "so that the sound design could take centre-stage" (Laced; corrected from 'desert'). Stjärnljus's 'use music fairly sparsely' quote is UNVERIFIED because the commentary captions could not be re-pulled. Little Nightmares 2: "The game is also quiet when it needs to be" (Shacknews). In Little Nightmares 1, Lilja used ambiences that are "really loud and prominent... most prominent during the early parts of the game" (The Sound Architect).

principles.principle: Footsteps are a speed-keyed, per-surface system with context transition sounds, not one sample played on a timer.
principles.evidence: INSIDE (Schmid, AES 2016 slides) uses footstep 'matrix' events keyed by speed: idle < 0.07, sneak < 0.37, walk < 0.70, jog < 0.92, run < 1.30, sprint >= 1.30 (engine units). Transitions choose context sounds: run->stop plays 'brake' and idle->jog plays 'takeoff_mf'. A wetness parameter decays toward 0 when dry and adds a wet layer on top. Limbo splits toe and heel contacts. Stray recorded foley for 28 surfaces. Planet of Lana: "Foley was one element that we could keep as extremely realistic" against surreal ambiences, and landings change with jump height ("a system that detects the height of the jump") (A Sound Effect, Ameglio).

principles.principle: Repeated footsteps get quieter over time so they don't fatigue the ear, and they recover on a new surface or after the character stands still.
principles.evidence: Limbo, from Andersen in Designing Sound 2011 (as corrected), uses two strategies. First, steps "start attenuating gradually after the boy has been moving continuously for a shorter period of time, and regain in amplitude when he's standing still". Second, steps on the same material attenuate "until he steps onto a new material whereby the amplitude gets a small boost". The range is "about 15dB in total, without taking distance based attenuation and active mixing into account". Andersen also did not normalise sounds; he stored each "at the level that I imagine is the maximum they will play back in the game" to keep the dynamics.

principles.principle: Keep the protagonist's sounds small and clear against heavy ambient beds to sell vulnerability. Show the character's growth through music and animation, not by changing the player's own sounds.
principles.evidence: Little Nightmares, Lilja: "Just the simple fact that Six is barefoot adds a lot to the feeling of being small and vulnerable, and we tried to emphasize that contrast by mixing quite distinct footstep sounds with heavy background ambient sounds". Mervik: "the light slap of her bare feet fighting to be heard amidst the heavy, industrial machinery of The Maw". Six's late-game confidence came "through the music".

principles.principle: Breathing is a sequencer that drives animation. The audio callback moves the body, the breath rate locks to the footsteps, and the breath intensity tracks exertion and danger.
principles.evidence: INSIDE (Schmid, AES 2016 and Wwise Tour 2016 decks): a Voice Sequencer alternates inhale and exhale. "Recorded breath sounds have varying durations. Continuous sequencing results in natural, uneven breathing pattern". "Voice intensity = lowpass filtered exhaustion". Intensity clamps can be "interpolated in space" ("Useful for indicating proximity to danger") or relax over time. Each breath fires a callback that "controls additive breathing animation, affecting boy pose". When running, breathing locks to "1 breath for every 2 steps" (right foot at phase 0.0, left at 0.5) using DJ-style beat matching. Jumping holds the breath. On landing, "soft impact: normal exhale, hard impact: grunt" (Wwise Tour 2016 deck, per correction). Playdead's animation slides list 'breathe' and 'look around' as additive layers over locomotion.

principles.principle: With no HUD, audio carries threat state. Use one stem set per threat, crossfade the stems by state, and when the player hides, drop everything except the threat and the player's body.
principles.evidence: Little Nightmares, Lilja (The Sound Architect): "each enemy has their own music track that adapts to their state"; "we simply crossfade to a different stem mix depending on the state of the enemy... there is no tempo syncing going on, the stems just keep looping". With several enemies, "the system looks for the currently most aggressive one in the room". In the listening state, "all background sounds and music are quickly pulled down to a minimum to give full focus to the sounds coming from the enemy and from Six, including her heartbeats." Enemy breathing was used to signal presence when "the camera... doesn't always allow for you to see the enemy". Letting the breathing show enemy state was an idea they "tried", and players misread it as scent-tracking ("sounds can also be unintentionally misleading").

principles.principle: Sound announces a hazard before you can see it, goes quiet once it is passed, and marks surviving it.
principles.evidence: Limbo (Andersen, as summarised in the Playdead dossier): sounds are pushed forward for approaching hazards "before visual revelation, then silenced them as players passed", and there is a "stinger-like sound, triggered when the boy survives" the rotating rooms. Little Nightmares: "if an enemy screams, it's because they are alerted to your presence and ... most likely chasing you" (Lilja).

principles.principle: Sounds that carry through walls tell the player which off-screen threat it is and roughly where it is. Wider rooms make this necessary.
principles.evidence: Little Nightmares: the Chef's coughs were loud enough to carry through walls and became "sonic identifiers". The Janitor's footsteps are mixed with rattling keys. Lilja was inspired by Bresson's off-screen guard sounds in A Man Escaped: "Doing this kind of thing in a game requires a lot of work since it radically affects gameplay. All disciplines need to be in sync about it." Rule: "Each sound should have a clear function and when possible also give vital information" (creaky floors attract enemies).

principles.principle: Standing still is a verb. Silence and stillness should reveal more of the world.
principles.evidence: Planet of Lana (Ameglio, A Sound Effect): "if the player stays still (doesn't move at all), they'll start to hear new sounds being introduced into the ambience". The cost was "double the amount of ambiences for each biome". No threshold time was published. Little Nightmares' listening-state duck and Limbo's notional silence make the same point from the threat side.

principles.principle: Clarity over density. Cut layers until several sources stay readable together, and never bury a sound the player has to read under sound design.
principles.evidence: Planet of Lana: the flying robot started "way more noisy". When several flew at once, "We had a lot of layers for the flying sound and we just got rid of 80% of them". In QA, players could not tell "where the pitch was" in the audio puzzles, so the tones became clean pipe-organ notes; Ameglio thinks the reverb is done in FMOD (hedged, per correction).

principles.principle: Death and respawn must not break the audio. Room tone and voice state carry on through the reload (the "illusion of no time passing").
principles.evidence: INSIDE (Wwise Tour 2016): "Audio should retain state and continue during load. When reload is complete, audio should switch to new state instantly. We call this a scene change." Audio commands that pile up during the load all execute when the fade-in starts. This needed a 2 MB command queue, and the audio buffer was raised from 512 to 1024 samples because 512 glitched. Little Nightmares 2: Roussel (Bandai Namco producer, not Tarsier) cites "a nearly immediate respawn" on Xbox Series X|S. The 'music will continue playing underneath' quote attributed to Andersen is UNVERIFIED.

principles.principle: Write a state record for each character and fire every sound when that state changes, scaled by the physics behind it.
principles.evidence: INSIDE: an Effect Analyzer writes a double-buffered Effect State each frame (animation, ground, material, velocity, landing impact, water, wetness). Sounds fire on a state change, e.g. "Set land impact parameter to 70, Play land sound", with impact "based on velocity in the direction of surface normal" (AES 2016). Cloth sound came from geometry: "Tracking a single elbow was enough." Little Nightmares: doors "can be pushed fast or slow, which the audio also needs to adapt to". Lilja built creak loops up to 30 s long and modulated them by door speed.

principles.principle: Give the companion a voice that answers, and have the protagonist answer back. Tone of voice carries the bond, not confirmation beeps.
principles.evidence: Planet of Lana (Eriksson, Game Developer): "In the beginning we weren't going to have any dialogue... we decided that we needed one more layer of emotional expression for it to work." Commentary (UNVERIFIED, captions not re-pulled): "Lana and Mui is always communicating... that's also why it's so important that Lana got a voice of her own and that Mui answers her." Mui's voice was performed by Ameglio and pitch-shifted (A Sound Effect).

principles.principle: Decide early how audio behaves on each target platform, and verify it by measurement, not by ear in the editor.
principles.evidence: Little Nightmares, Lilja's stated regret: "we didn't do more thorough research about the audio API's of the different platforms ... early on". INSIDE only found glitches by recording console output over S/PDIF and reading spectrograms. INSIDE also chose formats per content (PCM for music, Vorbis quality 10 for the rest). Stray shipped on the engine's own audio with no middleware. Phone and laptop speaker mixing is a GAP: none of the dossiers gives speaker-specific EQ, loudness or frequency targets. The ports (INSIDE iOS, Planet of Lana mobile, Little Nightmares mobile) document controls, memory and thermals, not the mix.

targets.metric: Footstep speed bands
targets.target: At least 3 bands (sneak/walk/run, or the hold-to-move equivalents), keyed off actual velocity rather than input. Add dedicated start ('takeoff') and stop ('brake') transition sounds.
targets.basis: INSIDE uses 6 bands (idle < 0.07, sneak < 0.37, walk < 0.70, jog < 0.92, run < 1.30, sprint >= 1.30) plus transition events (AES 2016). Cutting to 3 for a hold-to-move game is my derivation, not a published number.

targets.metric: Adaptive footstep attenuation range
targets.target: Up to about 15 dB total. Steps fade during continuous movement and recover when idle; steps on the same material fade and get a small boost on a new surface.
targets.basis: Limbo, Andersen: "about 15dB in total, without taking distance based attenuation and active mixing into account" (Designing Sound 2011).

targets.metric: Surface count
targets.target: 1 distinct footstep surface per floor material that actually appears. For the current three rooms, that means the corridor, Records Access and Service Junction floors, plus any grating or water. Add a surface only when a room adds a material.
targets.basis: Stray shipped 28 recorded surfaces across 12 chapters. No source gives a per-room ratio, so the per-material rule is derived. Treat 28 as a ceiling, not a target.

targets.metric: Running breath-to-step ratio
targets.target: 1 breath per 2 footsteps while running, eased into phase gradually (not snapped). Inhale/exhale lengths vary so the walking rhythm is uneven.
targets.basis: INSIDE AES 2016 and Wwise Tour 2016 decks, verified in both.

targets.metric: Landing response
targets.target: Landing sound volume/parameter scales with velocity along the surface normal. Above a hard-impact threshold the engineer grunts; below it they exhale normally. The threshold is a tuning value with no published number.
targets.basis: INSIDE example landImpact 70 (AES 2016); soft exhale vs hard grunt (Wwise Tour 2016); Planet of Lana's jump-height-dependent landings.

targets.metric: Respawn audio gap
targets.target: 0 ms of silence or room-tone restart across a death/respawn. Room tone, any threat stem and WOLF's vocal state keep playing; new-state changes apply at fade-in.
targets.basis: INSIDE scene-change design ("illusion of no time passing"). The 0 ms target restates their rule; actual INSIDE respawn duration is UNVERIFIED.

targets.metric: Simultaneous-threat readability
targets.target: The purge sentry's loop must stay identifiable with 3 instances audible at once. Layer count gets cut until that passes, not raised.
targets.basis: Planet of Lana cut 80% of the flying-robot layers after several on screen became unreadable. The '3 at once' test case comes from the Planet of Lana dossier's own avoid-list, not a measured figure.

targets.metric: Music density
targets.target: Music plays only at authored story or threat beats. Everything else is room tone. As a sanity check, Limbo used 6 tracks across a 3-4 h game, so expect at most one music cue per room in the current slice, and often none.
targets.basis: Limbo (HG101 track count); Planet of Lana spotted score; Little Nightmares threat-only adaptive tracks. The per-room cap is my derivation.

targets.metric: Listening-state duck
targets.target: When the engineer is hidden while a threat is alert, pull room tone and music down quickly to a near-floor level. Keep the threat, WOLF and the engineer's breath and heartbeat. Exact dB and fade time are UNVERIFIED: tune by ear and on device.
targets.basis: Little Nightmares (Lilja): "quickly pulled down to a minimum". No numbers were published.

targets.metric: Audio buffer for scene changes
targets.target: If reload causes clicks, raise the output buffer before cutting content. INSIDE moved from 512 to 1024 samples.
targets.basis: INSIDE Wwise Tour 2016. How this maps to Godot's output latency setting is not covered by the dossiers.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Add an engineer footstep system to the procedural bank. Generate per-surface step recipes (metal grate, deck plate, records-floor tile; wet as an overlay parameter that decays) with several deterministic variants each, played in round-robin. Trigger steps from the actor's real velocity and walk phase in m0_actor.gd, not from a timer. Include a 'takeoff' sound on hold-to-move start and a 'brake' sound on release. Put steps on their own player(s) so they never steal one of the 4 shared Effects voices.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Footstep variety, speed-keyed matrices and transition sounds are the best-documented 'real feel' mechanic in the corpus (INSIDE, Limbo, Stray, Planet of Lana). The game currently has none, and 4 round-robin voices would be starved by steps on top of impacts.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Directly implements 'real feel: footsteps per surface, weight'. Hold-to-move already gives continuous velocity to key off. Per-room surfaces fit the wider-rooms decision.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Give each room a continuous room-tone loop (hum, ventilation, drip) on a player that lives above the room scene. At walk-through doorways it crossfades rather than cuts, and it is never stopped by death or reload. Separate it from the pressure-gauge hum and hiss, which are puzzle telemetry.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Every reference game makes ambience the default soundtrack, and Little Nightmares puts it loudest early. INSIDE's scene-change rule keeps it running through death. At the moment hum and hiss only exist as gauge feedback, so most of the game sits in digital silence rather than the authored kind.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Implements 'room tone' and supports 'walk-through doorways'. A death that drops evidence still needs the world to keep sounding, so it doesn't feel like a menu reload.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Make death a 'scene change' for audio. Do not call stop_all() on death. Freeze new triggers during the fade, queue any state changes and apply them at fade-in, and keep room tone and WOLF's last vocal state playing. If the evidence drop needs a cue, use one short diegetic sound (case latch or scattered papers) rather than a silence or jingle.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE engineered continuity explicitly ("illusion of no time passing"). Little Nightmares and Limbo reviewers forgave frequent deaths because retries were fast and seamless.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Supports the decided death model. The research's concern is that a penalty plus a hard audio cut together reads as punishment. Continuity softens the cost without removing it.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Test the mix on device before claiming it works. Play the current three rooms on a laptop's built-in speakers and on a phone speaker, and write down which cues disappear. The thud is a 60 Hz sine and the boom sub sweeps 55 to 30 Hz, so check whether they still read through their noise and click layers. Confirm Godot's web and mobile audio behaviour (buffer, latency, autoplay unlock) now, not at export time.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Lilja's stated regret was researching platform audio late, and INSIDE found glitches only by measuring. The dossiers contain NO speaker-specific mixing evidence, so this has to be measured locally. The low-frequency concern is general audio knowledge, not dossier evidence.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Supports desktop, controller and phone touch, and follows AGENT.md's rule to separate headless tests from hands-on device tests.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Add an engineer breathing sequencer on the Voice bus. Alternate inhale and exhale variants of uneven length. Intensity is a low-pass-filtered exertion value from movement plus a per-area clamp near danger such as the sentry lane. When running, lock to 1 breath per 2 steps and ease into phase. On landing from the walkable height change, exhale for a soft landing and grunt for a hard one. Each breath fires a signal that drives a small additive chest/shoulder offset on the engineer.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's breathing system is the corpus's clearest case of audio-driven animation and of signalling danger without a HUD ("Useful for indicating proximity to danger").
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Implements 'breathing' and 'weight' from the real-feel decision. One walkable height change per room gives the landing hook. Procedural breath noise is untested in the corpus (see conflicts).

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Build a double-buffered effect state on the engineer and WOLF (surface, speed band, landing impact along the normal, wetness, engaged-in-USE) that the impact kit and sfx_bank read on state changes. Move the scattered sfx_bank.play() calls in main.gd behind it where they describe body events.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's Effect Analyzer splits 'state wrong' bugs from 'sound wrong' bugs and scales impacts by physics. main.gd currently fires roughly 25 hand-placed play() calls.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Makes the shake, hit-stop, flash and procedural-sound kit coherent and gives footsteps, breathing and look-at one shared source.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Give the purge sentry (and future room threats) a per-state loop set (idle-working, alerted, pursuit) crossfaded by volume tweens with no tempo sync, plus a 'most aggressive threat in room' selector. Add a listening-state duck snapshot on the bus layout when the engineer is hidden from an alert threat. Pair any audible 'it stopped and is listening' tell with one visible tell, and check every tell against what the sentry can actually sense.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Lilja's state-stem crossfade and listening duck are cheap and proven. His warning that breathing was misread as smell-tracking means audio tells must not suggest senses the AI lacks.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Fits the existing sentry_brain.gd states and the no-HUD direction. Wider rooms will hide the sentry off-camera, so audio has to carry it.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Switch WOLF and room threats to positional players (AudioStreamPlayer2D) with distinct 'sonic identifiers' that carry through walls (servo whine, claw ticks on grating, the sentry's mechanism). Then when WOLF scouts or leads ahead off-screen, the player can hear where he is and what he is doing.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Little Nightmares used off-screen sonic identifiers (Chef cough, Janitor keys) because the camera framed less than the room. Planet of Lana needed an off-screen status icon for its companion; audio can do part of that job without a HUD.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Directly serves 'WOLF's own routes (scouting, leading)' and 1.5-2 screen rooms. It keeps WOLF independent but legible.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Make USE-hold interactions sound different by input. A slow hold on a valve, bolt or door gives a quiet continuous creak or ratchet whose pitch and volume follow progress. A tap or fast action is louder and sharper. Only make 'loud attracts the sentry' true if the detection model really implements it.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Little Nightmares modulated 30-second creak loops by door speed. Lilja's 'creaky floors attract enemies' turns a sound into information.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Uses the existing tap-or-hold USE (hold_use.gd) and the exit bolt and coolant relay without adding inputs.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Give WOLF a tonal vocal palette (servo-chirps, growl variants, a 'refuse' sound and an 'agree' sound) that answers the engineer's actions. Give the engineer short non-verbal replies (breath, a hum, a 'hey'). Route WOLF to the Voice bus, not Effects, so the player can balance companion voice separately.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Planet of Lana added voice because body language alone was not enough, and the bond was carried by Mui answering Lana. The game's only WOLF voice now is the growl on Effects.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Supports WOLF as an independent companion who agrees, disagrees or refuses, and WOLF memory gating (his tone can shift with how he was treated).

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Cut layers so sounds stay readable. Test the sentry, the door blast and the tank drop with all room loops running at once. Remove recipe layers until each event stays readable, especially through phone speakers. Make any audio cue a puzzle depends on the cleanest, most tonal sound in the mix.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Planet of Lana cut 80% of the robot layers and simplified its puzzle tones after QA.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Fits the procedural sfx_bank, where removing a layer is a code edit, and the decided impact kit.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Keep the Music bus mostly empty. Score only authored beats such as a WOLF memory moment or the junction's escape. Consider making at least one tense sequence music-free on purpose so the machinery carries it.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Limbo's six tracks, Planet of Lana's spotted score and music-free beach run, and Little Nightmares' threat-only adaptive music all point the same way.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Consistent with the current state (a Music bus exists, no music yet) and procedural audio. It avoids a looping score that would have to survive death and respawn.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Add footstep fatigue attenuation (continuous-movement fade with idle recovery, and same-material fade with a boost on a new surface) within about 15 dB. Consider moving from 'normalise every clip to -6 dB' to authoring each recipe's peak at its intended in-game level, so relative loudness lives in the recipe rather than in scattered volume_db values.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Limbo's passive mix and Andersen's 'store at the maximum level it will play' rule both protect dynamic range across a long play session.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Builds on the footstep system. The normalisation change is optional because the current volume_db offsets get to the same place, just less clearly.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Add a stand-still listening layer. After the engineer has been motionless for a tuned time, fade in an extra ambient layer per room (distant machinery, WOLF breathing, something behind a wall), which can also carry environmental evidence clues.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Planet of Lana's 'listening to the world' system makes stillness a verb. Its cost (double ambience per biome) is lower when ambience is procedural.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Fits horror pacing and the evidence CASE: a clue that only appears when you stop and listen. No dossier publishes a threshold time.

conflicts_with_decisions: Procedural audio vs the 'real feel' goal: every reference game builds body sound from recordings. INSIDE is 'sample-based with procedural selection and sequencing, not synthesis' (Schmid's 2019 talk mentions real-time synthesis only as a later direction). Planet of Lana kept foley 'extremely realistic'. Stray recorded foley for 28 surfaces. The corpus has no shipped example of fully synthesised footsteps, breathing or voice reading as 'real'. Procedural synthesis is well supported for ambience, machines and impacts (Lana's finale beam was about 90% Serum synth, per Ameglio's hedged recollection). The research leans toward a hybrid: procedural room tone, machines and impacts, with procedural selection and sequencing over small sets of body sounds, possibly recorded. Nathanial decides; recorded audio would need entries in the asset register.

Death drops unsecured evidence: none of the four companies' audio or respawn pipelines attach a cost to death. INSIDE's continuity design assumes death is free. The research doesn't say the penalty is wrong, but it says a penalty plus an audio cut or loss jingle will read as punishment. If the drop stays, keep the audio continuous and the loss cue diegetic and short.

Mixing for laptop and phone speakers has no evidence base in these dossiers. None of the mobile ports (INSIDE iOS, Planet of Lana mobile, Little Nightmares mobile) documents its mix. Any target there (low-end cut-off, loudness, mono fold-down) is UNVERIFIED and must come from device testing, not from this research. The current mono 22.05 kHz bank is not contradicted by any source.

WOLF's procedural voice and the decision that WOLF is independent: Lilja's warning applies. Players believe any sound that implies a sense or intent (breathing read as smelling). If WOLF's audible reactions suggest he noticed or decided something the AI did not, players will read that as his choice. Every WOLF and sentry sound has to match the real behaviour model, which limits free-form procedural variation in WOLF's voice.

syn.dimension: MOBILE AND INPUT: touch schemes for side-scrollers, one-button interaction, readability at phone size, performance budgets, session length, controller parity

principles.principle: Treat every finger the same and combine them in one touch state machine. Do not depend on a fixed invisible d-pad that loses the thumb.
principles.evidence: INSIDE iOS (Gjøl, 'INSIDE Shipping on iOS', Digital Dragons 2018, https://github.com/playdeadgames/publications/blob/master/INSIDE/inside_shipping_on_ios.pdf): "all touches/fingers are treated equally and a state-machine is tracking their individual behavior from touch-start to touch-end. Their states will all be combined. If one finger moves right and another left, the boy will stand still". The same deck says "Robust: Hold device with a thumb ON-SCREEN". Limbo iOS (Game Informer, https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2013/07/03/limbo-ios-impressions.aspx) used an invisible d-pad on the left side, and the main complaint was "Sometimes the boy would just stop moving mid-jog and I would have to reset my thumb". That made timing puzzles "notably harder", and the reviewer's verdict was "the inferior choice... but it's far from unplayable." Correction applied: the line 'swipe left and right to move... tap/hold' on the INSIDE App Store page comes from a customer review, not from Playdead.

principles.principle: On touch, turn USE into a gesture aimed at the object, or a context button. Keep the interaction animation as short as it can be while still reading as an action. Never auto-complete it.
principles.evidence: INSIDE iOS made two separate changes (the slide conflation is corrected here). (1) In 'Make it easier to play on touch', "Swipe _towards_ object to grab" applies only to things that block movement and was "very useful underwater". (2) In 'Make it feel better', they "Tried auto-complete, ends up waiting for triggered animation to end. loses feeling of interaction :(" and switched to the "Short as possible animation while still prioritising the feeling of interaction". This started with the jetcrate and spread to levers, windows, the raft and secrets. It was a "Very painful change, since we really liked the weight of the controller input", and it hurt most on timing-critical beats ("Sentry gun in city, Sentry gun in sewers"). Planet of Lana mobile (App Store 1.0.5 notes, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/planet-of-lana/id6739130049) fixed "button disappearance during environmental interactions", which shows its touch interface uses contextual on-screen buttons.

principles.principle: Keep the verb set tiny. Fit more meaning into it with tap versus hold, not with more buttons. Never require simultaneous presses or long holds to survive.
principles.evidence: Per Game Developer's report of Carlsen's GDC Europe 2010 talk, Limbo's director set the rule that the game uses only directional control and two buttons (jump and grab) (attribution corrected). Planet of Lana (Wishfully, Xbox Wire, https://news.xbox.com/en-us/?p=185820) maps two companion verbs to one button: "A tap will make Mui stay in one spot, while holding the button down will get her to follow you". Little Nightmares II was criticised for hold-to-grip: "you must hold down the button all the while otherwise you'll lose your grip" and "Hand cramp is a real issue" (PlayStation LifeStyle, attribution corrected). Push Square wrote "we experienced a lot of cramping in our hands" and "uncomfortably long trigger holds" (LN1). Windows Central said Planet of Lana's controls "require you to hold them down, sometimes for long periods of time" and the game had no hold-to-toggle at launch. Family Gaming Database lists Planet of Lana as 'No Simultaneous Buttons' and 'Rapid Repeated Pressing Optional'. Tarsier cut a whistle-to-herd verb (relayed by level designer Matthew Compher via Push Square).

principles.principle: Ship more than one input mode on mobile, and support a physical controller on every port.
principles.evidence: The Little Nightmares mobile port (Playdigious, 11-12 Dec 2023, https://en.bandainamcoent.eu/node/8904) has three modes: Controller Mode (MFi), Standard Mode "with the various controls appearing on the screen", and Immersive Mode for "greater immersion". The claim that Immersive Mode has no on-screen buttons is UNVERIFIED (correction). Planet of Lana mobile promises a "Revamped interface – exclusive mobile UI with complete touch control", and its 1.0.4 notes mention an 'immersive mode', a 'tap' icon and switching control between Lana and Mui with a Mui 'Go to' action. The exact gestures are UNVERIFIED. The App Store listings for Limbo, INSIDE and Planet of Lana all list PlayStation, Xbox or MFi controller support. iMore recommends playing INSIDE on Apple TV with a controller.

principles.principle: Readability at phone size: thumbs and buttons hide the art, and dark scenes go unreadable on a phone. Brighten deliberately, ground the characters with shadows, and keep the action clear of the thumb zones.
principles.evidence: On INSIDE iOS: "Covering up any element of the screen with your thumb does a disservice to Inside's immaculate visual language" (AppUnwrapper, https://www.appunwrapper.com/2017/12/29/playdeads-inside-ios-review/). iMore found it "so dark that I can't tell whether there is something to interact with" (https://www.imore.com/playdeads-inside-review-there-beauty-death), and called press-and-hold-near-object unintuitive. Playdead fitted a polynomial brightness curve to "Get it BRIGHT enough" for outdoor phone use (Gjøl 2018). INSIDE also uses a constant "fake ambient color, that's always there, so we can see it in the dark", plus a rim light and blob shadow decals under the feet (GDC 2016 rendering deck). Little Nightmares players misjudged depth: "you'll inevitably misjudge your position and perish" (Push Square LN1).

principles.principle: Set the phone performance budget from comfort and memory, not from desktop frame rate. Prewarm everything that can hitch.
principles.evidence: From Gjøl 2018: the first INSIDE iOS proof of concept ran "around 30fps". An iPhone X "can run at 60fps with no framedrops but gets too hot for puny human comfort", at about 40 °C, so they targeted comfort. A runtime overlay showed the CPU frequency scale. They preloaded and prewarmed every shader variant collected from playthroughs. Memory was the hard limit: about 900 MB worst case, against about 600 MB allowed on 1 GB devices and about 1200 MB on 2 GB devices. The App Store cannot filter by RAM, so INSIDE shipped the first part free with an in-app unlock and a 'sorry' scene on unsupported devices. Console budget (Unite 2016): 16.6 ms per frame and zero per-frame garbage. Stray's PC stutter came from UE4 shader compilation (Kotaku citing Digital Foundry). Planet of Lana shipped Xbox One and One X below its target resolution at launch (Windows Central). Store sizes: Limbo 141.6 MB, INSIDE 739 MB, Planet of Lana 3.1 GB (iOS 15.6+, A12 or later).

principles.principle: Short, self-contained chunks with dense automatic checkpoints suit mobile sessions. The whole game stays a few hours, with no padding.
principles.evidence: INSIDE: "Each Puzzle span around 100 meters or 1-3min of gameplay" (Unite 2016). Limbo's checkpoints keep deaths from "setting you back more than twenty-ish seconds of progress" (HG101 reviewer estimate, corrected quote). Family Gaming Database defines 'Bank Progress With Frequent Checkpoints' as losing under 5 minutes and lists it for Planet of Lana. Little Nightmares II: Roussel (Bandai Namco producer, attribution corrected) describes "a nearly immediate respawn" on Xbox Series X|S. Lengths: LN1 three to four hours, Planet of Lana around 4-6 hours, Limbo 3-4 hours. Mervik: "We never really wanted to make a long game". Planet of Lana funnel on Steam (corrected): about 21% of players who started never unlocked 'A new friend' (meeting the companion), and about 40% of starters finished.

principles.principle: Controller and touch parity means the same content and gameplay. Accept small touch-specific tuning, and guard visual parity with automated playthrough screenshots.
principles.evidence: INSIDE iOS: "Same gameplay, levels, rendering-pipeline... Slightly tweaked gameplay to make touch-controls work better." A QA tool took a screenshot "every 5 meters from a playthrough" at "around 1300 locations" and diffed them against references (Gjøl 2018). Playdead skipped the Vita touchpad because Patti said they "didn't feel it would suit Limbo at all" (corrected quote, via Wikipedia). Pocket Gamer on Planet of Lana mobile: "nothing's been stripped or simplified". Accessibility parity: Planet of Lana launched with only a QTE toggle and was criticised for it. FGDB now lists keyboard-only play, input documentation and adjustable touch sensitivity, but not remapping (corrected).

principles.principle: Use haptics to carry state the screen does not show, and keep them optional.
principles.evidence: Little Nightmares chases: "the controller pulsates in unison with your pounding heartbeat" (Push Square LN1). Planet of Lana lists 'Vibration Optional' (FGDB). No dossier gives intensity or duration numbers.

targets.metric: Progress lost on death (time back to the last safe point)
targets.target: About 20 s or less of replay in normal rooms. Never more than 5 min anywhere.
targets.basis: Limbo's 'twenty-ish seconds' (HG101 reviewer estimate, not a measurement) and FGDB's under-5-minute definition of frequent checkpoints. No developer-published number exists. Respawn duration itself is UNVERIFIED in every dossier, so measure WOLF//OVERRIDE's own.

targets.metric: Length of one room or puzzle chunk (a mobile session unit)
targets.target: 1-3 min of play per room. A 1.5-2 screen room should hold one puzzle beat.
targets.basis: INSIDE: each puzzle spans about 100 m or 1-3 min (Unite 2016 slides, verified).

targets.metric: Frame time on the target phone
targets.target: 16.6 ms (60 fps) is the aim. Use a 30 fps fallback if thermals require it. No first-use shader or asset hitches.
targets.basis: INSIDE console budget of 16.6 ms; the INSIDE iOS proof of concept at ~30 fps; Playdead prewarming every shader variant; Stray's PC stutter from shader compilation.

targets.metric: Device surface temperature during sustained play
targets.target: Stays below about 40 °C after a long session, for example 30+ min on the slowest supported phone. The session length is a suggestion, not from a source.
targets.basis: Gjøl 2018: about 40 °C felt uncomfortable, and they targeted 'human comfort' over the device spec.

targets.metric: Peak app memory
targets.target: Well under 600 MB, the ceiling Playdead had on 1 GB devices. Pick the minimum device to match. Planet of Lana requires iOS 15.6+ and A12; Limbo and INSIDE require iOS 13+.
targets.basis: Gjøl 2018 memory table (verified); App Store listings.

targets.metric: Install size
targets.target: Stay in the Limbo range (141.6 MB) rather than INSIDE (739 MB) or Planet of Lana (3.1 GB). Treat size as a soft target.
targets.basis: App Store listings fetched 2026-10-10.

targets.metric: Simultaneous inputs and holds required to progress or survive
targets.target: 0 simultaneous-button requirements. 0 sustained holds needed to avoid death. Every long hold has a toggle.
targets.basis: FGDB 'No Simultaneous Buttons' (Planet of Lana); cramp complaints about LN1 and LN2; Windows Central on Planet of Lana's long holds without a toggle.

targets.metric: Input parity
targets.target: 100% of essential actions work on touch, controller and keyboard alone, plus controller support on mobile.
targets.basis: Every shipped port in the corpus (Limbo, INSIDE, LN1 mobile, Planet of Lana mobile) supports MFi/PS/Xbox controllers; FGDB 'Keyboard Alone'.

targets.metric: Visual parity checks between desktop and phone
targets.target: An automated screenshot at fixed intervals along a recorded playthrough of every room (Playdead used every 5 m and about 1300 locations for the whole game), diffed per platform.
targets.basis: Gjøl 2018 (verified).

targets.metric: Time to meet the companion
targets.target: Within the first room or chunk.
targets.basis: Planet of Lana: about 21% of starters stopped before 'A new friend' (corrected Steam funnel). This is correlation, not proof of cause.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Check on a real phone that the engineer can hold LEFT or RIGHT and tap USE, or hold USE to CRANK, at the same time. The current touch layer is Control Buttons (apps/game/scripts/main.gd, _bind_touch_button with button_down/up calling Input.action_press). With default touch-to-mouse emulation, Godot GUI buttons may not track a second finger. If it fails, replace the layer with a per-touch-index handler (InputEventScreenTouch/Drag) or TouchScreenButton, and combine all active touches as INSIDE did.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's touch scheme rests on 'all touches/fingers are treated equally' and on a resting thumb. Limbo's d-pad dropping the thumb mid-jog was its main touch complaint.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Applies to the current three rooms (hold-to-move plus USE tap or hold, valve CRANK) and to the planned wider rooms. Only a device test can settle it; a headless test cannot.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Keep the current camera drop for touch (GAMEPLAY_CAMERA_Y_TOUCH places feet above the button tops at screen y 345). Add a check that no USE target, hazard tell or WOLF tell sits in the button bands (left/right buttons x 32-238, USE x 773-928, y 345-435 on the 960x540 canvas) at any point in the new 1.5-2 screen rooms and their height changes.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: Reviewers said thumbs covering INSIDE's art hurt it. LN depth misreads killed players. A walkable height change can push the floor line into the button band.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Wider rooms with one walkable height change each. The existing touch camera offset is the right base to build on.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Add a phone brightness pass. Use a raised gamma or brightness curve for mobile, a constant 'fake ambient' minimum on the engineer and WOLF, and soft contact shadows under feet and paws at the height changes.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: iMore could not tell what was interactive on a dark iPhone screen even after Playdead's brightness curve. INSIDE used fake ambient light and blob shadows to keep characters readable.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Painterly 2.5D look; wider rooms with height changes; Godot gl_compatibility renderer (CanvasModulate and Light2D are cheap).

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Keep USE as the only interaction verb on every platform. On touch, show it as a contextual button (as now: USE, CRANK, DROP, CONTINUE). Prototype 'swipe toward the object' for objects that block movement, such as doors and the exit bolt. Shorten touch-triggered interaction animations and do not auto-complete holds.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE rejected auto-complete because it 'loses feeling of interaction' and shortened animations instead. Planet of Lana mobile uses contextual buttons that appear per interaction.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: One USE (tap or hold) and the planned single tool. Map the tool to USE in context, not to a new button.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Add hold-to-toggle options for move and for USE-hold (CRANK), and make any USE-hold progress-safe on release. Never make a sustained hold the only way to avoid death.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: LN1 and LN2 hand cramp; Planet of Lana's long holds with no toggle drew criticism at launch.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: Hold-to-move, the USE hold, and the AGENT.md rule that saved preferences and bindings are validated.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Give each new room one puzzle beat of about 1-3 min. Put a safe point at every walk-through doorway so a phone session can stop at any room boundary. Autosave on room entry, which already exists per main.gd, and on securing evidence.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's 1-3 min puzzle chunks; Limbo's 'twenty-ish seconds' checkpoint estimate; FGDB's under-5-minute bar.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: 1.5-2 screen rooms with walk-through doorways, and safe points that secure evidence.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Make the respawn a continuous scene change: fade, reload only the room's gameplay layer, keep room tone and WOLF's audio state playing, and resume. Time it on a phone.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.why: INSIDE's 'illusion of no time passing' and LN2's 'nearly immediate respawn' are why frequent deaths were forgiven. Phones load more slowly than desktops.
recommendations_for_wolf_override.fits_decisions: The death model (dropping unsecured evidence) and procedural room tone.

recommendations_for_wolf_override.change: Set a mobile performance gate: 60 fps target with a 30 fps option (the settings already offer 30/60), a sustained-play thermal test (surface under about 40 °C), peak memory logged, shader and particle prewarm at room load, and a debug overlay with frame time.
